MeasurableSpace.invariants.comment:
Given a self-map `f : α → α`,
`invariants f` is the σ-algebra of measurable sets that are invariant under `f`.

A set `s` is `(invariants f)`-measurable
iff it is meaurable w.r.t. the canonical σ-algebra on `α` and `f ⁻¹' s = s`.
MeasurableSpace.invariants.fullDefinition: def invariants [m : MeasurableSpace α] (f : α → α) : MeasurableSpace α :=   { m ⊓ ⟨fun s ↦ f ⁻¹' s = s, by simp, by simp, fun f hf ↦ by simp [hf]⟩ with     MeasurableSet' := fun s ↦ MeasurableSet[m] s ∧ f ⁻¹' s = s }

explanatories.Subtype.map: This definition pertains to the concept of limiting the scope of a function to include only elements from a subtype.
explanatories.Prod.map: A mapping function transforms a pair of elements by applying one function to the first element and another function to the second element.

exists_measurable_piecewise.comment:
Let `t i` be a nonempty countable family of measurable sets in `α`. Let `g i : α → β` be a
family of measurable functions such that `g i` agrees with `g j` on `t i ∩ t j`. Then there exists
a measurable function `f : α → β` that agrees with each `g i` on `t i`.

We only need the assumption `[Nonempty ι]` to prove `[Nonempty (α → β)]`.

IsCountablySpanning.comment:
We say that a collection of sets is countably spanning if a countable subset spans the
whole type. This is a useful condition in various parts of measure theory. For example, it is
a needed condition to show that the product of two collections generate the product sigma algebra,
see `generateFrom_prod_eq`.

explanatories.measurable_fst: The first component of a product between measurable spaces is a measurable function.
explanatories.measurable_snd: The second component of a product space is measurable regardless of the measurable structures of its components.
explanatories.Equiv.Set.prod: The definition establishes that the Cartesian product of two sets is equivalent to the product of their corresponding types when viewed as sets.
explanatories.MeasurableEquiv.Set.prod: The Cartesian product of two measurable sets is measurably equivalent to the product of their respective measurable spaces.
explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function constructs a sum type from an element of the first type.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection into the sum type combines an element from one type with the sum type, indicating it originates from the second type.
explanatories.MeasurableSet.prod: The Cartesian product of two measurable sets is also a measurable set.
explanatories.measurable_pi_apply: The evaluation of a function from a product of measurable spaces at a fixed point is measurable if each component space is endowed with its own measurable structure.
explanatories.measurable_pi_iff: A function is measurable if and only if, for every output type, its behavior when constrained to that output type is also measurable.
explanatories.Measurable.prod: If both components of a function from one measurable space to a product of two measurable spaces are measurable, then the entire function is also measurable.

MeasurableEquiv.sumPiEquivProdPi.fullDefinition: def sumPiEquivProdPi (α : δ ⊕ δ' → Type*) [∀ i, MeasurableSpace (α i)] :     (∀ i, α i) ≃ᵐ (∀ i, α (.inl i)) × ∀ i', α (.inr i') where   __ := Equiv.sumPiEquivProdPi α   measurable_toFun := by     apply Measurable.prod <;> rw [measurable_pi_iff] <;> rintro i <;> apply measurable_pi_apply   measurable_invFun := by     rw [measurable_pi_iff]; rintro (i | i)     · exact measurable_pi_iff.1 measurable_fst _     · exact measurable_pi_iff.1 measurable_snd _
MeasurableEquiv.sumPiEquivProdPi.description: There exists a measurable equivalence between the function type over a sum type and the product of function types over its components.

MeasurableEmbedding.schroederBernstein.fullDefinition: noncomputable def schroederBernstein {f : α → β} {g : β → α} (hf : MeasurableEmbedding f)     (hg : MeasurableEmbedding g) : α ≃ᵐ β := by   let F : Set α → Set α := fun A => (g '' (f '' A)ᶜ)ᶜ   -- We follow the proof of the usual SB theorem in mathlib,   -- the crux of which is finding a fixed point of this F.   -- However, we must find this fixed point manually instead of invoking Knaster-Tarski   -- in order to make sure it is measurable.   suffices Σ'A : Set α, MeasurableSet A ∧ F A = A by     rcases this with ⟨A, Ameas, Afp⟩     let B := f '' A     have Bmeas : MeasurableSet B := hf.measurableSet_image' Ameas     refine (MeasurableEquiv.sumCompl Ameas).symm.trans       (MeasurableEquiv.trans ?_ (MeasurableEquiv.sumCompl Bmeas))     apply MeasurableEquiv.sumCongr (hf.equivImage _)     have : Aᶜ = g '' Bᶜ := by       apply compl_injective       rw [← Afp]       simp     rw [this]     exact (hg.equivImage _).symm   have Fmono : ∀ {A B}, A ⊆ B → F A ⊆ F B := fun h =>     compl_subset_compl.mpr <| Set.image_subset _ <| compl_subset_compl.mpr <| Set.image_subset _ h   let X : ℕ → Set α := fun n => F^[n] univ   refine ⟨iInter X, ?_, ?_⟩   · apply MeasurableSet.iInter     intro n     induction' n with n ih     · exact MeasurableSet.univ     rw [Function.iterate_succ', Function.comp_apply]     exact (hg.measurableSet_image' (hf.measurableSet_image' ih).compl).compl   apply subset_antisymm   · apply subset_iInter     intro n     cases n     · exact subset_univ _     rw [Function.iterate_succ', Function.comp_apply]     exact Fmono (iInter_subset _ _)   rintro x hx ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩   rw [mem_iInter] at hx   apply hy   rw [hf.injective.injOn.image_iInter_eq]   rw [mem_iInter]   intro n   specialize hx n.succ   rw [Function.iterate_succ', Function.comp_apply] at hx   by_contra h   apply hx   exact ⟨y, h, rfl⟩
MeasurableEmbedding.schroederBernstein.description: The measurable Schröder-Bernstein Theorem asserts that if there are measurable embeddings in both directions between two measurable spaces, then there exists a measurable equivalence between them.

MeasurableSpace.generateMeasurableRec.code: MeasurableSpace.generateMeasurableRec.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set (Set α)) : (Quotient.out (aleph 1).ord).α → Set (Set α)
MeasurableSpace.generateMeasurableRec.comment:
Transfinite induction construction of the sigma-algebra generated by a set of sets `s`. At each
step, we add all elements of `s`, the empty set, the complements of already constructed sets, and
countable unions of already constructed sets. We index this construction by an ordinal `< ω₁`, as
this will be enough to generate all sets in the sigma-algebra.

This construction is very similar to that of the Borel hierarchy.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.Iio: This definition represents the set of elements that are strictly less than a given element in a preorder structure, creating a left-infinite and right-open interval.
explanatories.HasCompl.compl: A function that returns the complement of an element in a set or lattice structure.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.
explanatories.MeasurableSpace.GenerateMeasurable.compl: This theorem establishes that if a set is measurable with respect to a given family of sets, then its complement is also measurable with respect to that same family.

MeasurableSpace.generateMeasurableRec.fullDefinition: def generateMeasurableRec (s : Set (Set α)) : (ω₁ : Type u) → Set (Set α)   | i =>     let S := ⋃ j : Iio i, generateMeasurableRec s (j.1)     s ∪ {∅} ∪ compl '' S ∪ Set.range fun f : ℕ → S => ⋃ n, (f n).1   termination_by i => i   decreasing_by exact j.2
MeasurableSpace.generateMeasurableRec.description: This defines a process for generating a sigma-algebra from a collection of sets using transfinite induction indexed by ordinals, incorporating various set operations at each step.

IsPiSystem.comment:
A π-system is a collection of subsets of `α` that is closed under binary intersection of
non-disjoint sets. Usually it is also required that the collection is nonempty, but we don't do
that here.

IsPiSystem.fullDefinition: def IsPiSystem {α} (C : Set (Set α)) : Prop :=   ∀ᵉ (s ∈ C) (t ∈ C), (s ∩ t : Set α).Nonempty → s ∩ t ∈ C
IsPiSystem.description: This definition characterizes a collection of subsets as a π-system if it is closed under intersections of non-disjoint sets.

MeasurableSpace.DynkinSystem.restrictOn.fullDefinition: def restrictOn {s : Set α} (h : d.Has s) : DynkinSystem α where   -- Porting note(#12129): additional beta reduction needed   Has t := d.Has (t ∩ s)   has_empty := by simp [d.has_empty]   has_compl {t} hts := by     beta_reduce     have : tᶜ ∩ s = (t ∩ s)ᶜ \ sᶜ := Set.ext fun x => by by_cases h : x ∈ s <;> simp [h]     rw [this]     exact       d.has_diff (d.has_compl hts) (d.has_compl h)         (compl_subset_compl.mpr inter_subset_right)   has_iUnion_nat {f} hd hf := by     simp only []     rw [iUnion_inter]     refine d.has_iUnion_nat ?_ hf     exact hd.mono fun i j => Disjoint.mono inter_subset_left inter_subset_left
MeasurableSpace.DynkinSystem.restrictOn.description: The definition describes a method to create a new Dynkin system from an existing one by restricting it to sets that intersect with a specific set, provided that this set is included in the original Dynkin system.

      motive ∅ ⋯ →
        (∀ {a : Set α} (a_1 : GenerateHas s a), motive a a_1 → motive aᶜ ⋯) →
          (∀ {f : ℕ → Set α} (a : Pairwise (Disjoint on f)) (a_1 : ∀ (i : ℕ), GenerateHas s (f i)),

MeasurableSpace.DynkinSystem.generateFro.comment:
**Dynkin's π-λ theorem**:
Given a collection of sets closed under binary intersections, then the Dynkin system it
generates is equal to the σ-algebra it generates.
This result is known as the π-λ theorem.
A collection of sets closed under binary intersection is called a π-system (often requiring
additionally that it is non-empty, but we drop this condition in the formalization).

MeasureTheory.IsSetSemiring.diffFinset.comment:
In a semi-ring of sets `C`, for all sets `s, t ∈ C`, `s \ t` is equal to a disjoint union of
finitely many sets in `C`. The finite set of sets in the union is not unique, but this definition
gives an arbitrary `Finset (Set α)` that satisfies the equality.

We remove the empty set to ensure that `t ∉ hC.diffFinset hs ht` even if `t = ∅`.

  {β : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace β] (f : α → β) : Prop
EventuallyMeasurable.comment:
We say a function is `EventuallyMeasurable` with respect to a given
σ-algebra `m` and σ-filter `l` if the preimage of any measurable set is equal to some
`m`-measurable set modulo `l`.
Warning: This is not always the same as being equal to some `m`-measurable function modulo `l`.
In general it is weaker. See `Measurable.eventuallyMeasurable_of_eventuallyEq`.
*TODO*: Add lemmas about when these are equivalent.

MeasureTheory.squareCylinders.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} (C : (i : ι) → Set (Set (α i))) :
  Set (Set ((i : ι) → α i))
MeasureTheory.squareCylinders.comment:
Given a finite set `s` of indices, a square cylinder is the product of a set `S` of
`∀ i : s, α i` and of `univ` on the other indices. The set `S` is a product of sets `t i` such that
for all `i : s`, `t i ∈ C i`.
`squareCylinders` is the set of all such squareCylinders.

MeasureTheory.IsProjectiveMeasureFamily.comment:
A family of measures indexed by finite sets of `ι` is projective if, for finite sets `J ⊆ I`,
the projection from `∀ i : I, α i` to `∀ i : J, α i` maps `P I` to `P J`.

MeasureTheory.IsProjectiveMeasureFamily.description: A family of measures indexed by finite sets is defined as projective if the measure for a larger set can be consistently mapped to the measure for any of its finite subsets when projecting from the collective space to the smaller one.

def borelToRefl (e : Expr) (i : FVarId) : TacticM Unit := do   let te ← Lean.Elab.Term.exprToSyntax e   evalTactic <| ← `(tactic|     have := @BorelSpace.measurable_eq $te _ _ _)   try     liftMetaTactic fun m => return [← subst m i]   catch _ =>     let et ← synthInstance (← mkAppOptM ``TopologicalSpace #[e])     throwError m!"\       `‹TopologicalSpace {e}› := {et}

Mathlib.Tactic.Borelize.borelize.fullDefinition: def borelize (t : Term) : TacticM Unit := withMainContext <| do   let u ← mkFreshLevelMVar   let e ← withoutRecover <| Tactic.elabTermEnsuringType t (mkSort (mkLevelSucc u))   let i? ← findLocalDeclWithType? (← mkAppOptM ``MeasurableSpace #[e])   i?.elim (addBorelInstance e) (borelToRefl e)
Mathlib.Tactic.Borelize.borelize.description: This function attempts to establish the Borel space instance for a given type, either by replacing an existing measurable space assumption or by creating the necessary instances.

Mathlib.Tactic.Borelize.tacticBorelize__.comment:
The behaviour of `borelize α` depends on the existing assumptions on `α`.

- if `α` is a topological space with instances `[MeasurableSpace α] [BorelSpace α]`, then
  `borelize α` replaces the former instance by `borel α`;
- otherwise, `borelize α` adds instances `borel α : MeasurableSpace α` and `⟨rfl⟩ : BorelSpace α`.

Finally, `borelize α β γ` runs `borelize α; borelize β; borelize γ`.

Pi.opensMeasurableSpace.fullDefinition: instance Pi.opensMeasurableSpace {ι : Type*} {π : ι → Type*} [Countable ι]     [t' : ∀ i, TopologicalSpace (π i)] [∀ i, MeasurableSpace (π i)]     [∀ i, SecondCountableTopology (π i)] [∀ i, OpensMeasurableSpace (π i)] :     OpensMeasurableSpace (∀ i, π i) := by   constructor   have : Pi.topologicalSpace = .generateFrom { t | ∃ (s : ∀ a, Set (π a)) (i : Finset ι),       (∀ a ∈ i, s a ∈ countableBasis (π a)) ∧ t = pi (↑i) s } := by     simp only [funext fun a => @eq_generateFrom_countableBasis (π a) _ _, pi_generateFrom_eq]   rw [borel_eq_generateFrom_of_subbasis this]   apply generateFrom_le   rintro _ ⟨s, i, hi, rfl⟩   refine MeasurableSet.pi i.countable_toSet fun a ha => IsOpen.measurableSet ?_   rw [eq_generateFrom_countableBasis (π a)]   exact .basic _ (hi a ha)

pi.opens_measurable_space.fullDefinition: instance Pi.opensMeasurableSpace {ι : Type*} {π : ι → Type*} [Countable ι]     [t' : ∀ i, TopologicalSpace (π i)] [∀ i, MeasurableSpace (π i)]     [∀ i, SecondCountableTopology (π i)] [∀ i, OpensMeasurableSpace (π i)] :     OpensMeasurableSpace (∀ i, π i) := by   constructor   have : Pi.topologicalSpace = .generateFrom { t | ∃ (s : ∀ a, Set (π a)) (i : Finset ι),       (∀ a ∈ i, s a ∈ countableBasis (π a)) ∧ t = pi (↑i) s } := by     simp only [funext fun a => @eq_generateFrom_countableBasis (π a) _ _, pi_generateFrom_eq]   rw [borel_eq_generateFrom_of_subbasis this]   apply generateFrom_le   rintro _ ⟨s, i, hi, rfl⟩   refine MeasurableSet.pi i.countable_toSet fun a ha => IsOpen.measurableSet ?_   rw [eq_generateFrom_countableBasis (π a)]   exact .basic _ (hi a ha)
pi.opens_measurable_space.description: This construct defines a structure of opens measurable space for functions indexed by a countable type, ensuring that the function space inherits the opens measurable space properties from its components, each of which is equipped with a topological and measurable structure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_Ico_finite.comment:
Two finite measures on a Borel space are equal if they agree on all closed-open intervals.  If
`α` is a conditionally complete linear order with no top element,
`MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_Ico` is an extensionality lemma with weaker assumptions on `μ` and
`ν`.

measure_eq_measure_preimage_add_measure_tsum_Ico_zpow.{u_5} {α : Type u_5} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α)
  {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) {t : ℝ≥0} (ht : 1 < t) :
  μ s = μ (s ∩ f ⁻¹' {0}) + μ (s ∩ f ⁻¹' {⊤}) + ∑' (n : ℤ), μ (s ∩ f ⁻¹' Ico (↑t ^ n) (↑t ^ (n + 1)))
measure_eq_measure_preimage_add_measure_.comment:
One can cut out `ℝ≥0∞` into the sets `{0}`, `Ico (t^n) (t^(n+1))` for `n : ℤ` and `{∞}`. This
gives a way to compute the measure of a set in terms of sets on which a given function `f` does not
fluctuate by more than `t`.

explanatories.Set.Ioo: This definition specifies the set of elements that lie strictly between two given elements in a preorder structure, creating a left-open and right-open interval.
explanatories.Set.mem_iUnion: An element belongs to the union of a collection of sets if and only if it is an element of at least one set within that collection.
explanatories.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to a singleton set if and only if it is equal to the unique element in that set.
explanatories.neg_lt_self: This theorem states that if an element is greater than zero, then the negation of that element is less than the element itself in an additive group structure.
explanatories.Nat.cast_add_one_pos: This theorem demonstrates that the natural number cast of any non-negative integer, when increased by one, remains positive in types that satisfy specific algebraic and order properties.
explanatories.measure_Ioo_lt_top: This theorem states that the measure of the open interval defined by two points in a compact space with a locally finite measure is finite and less than infinity.
explanatories.Set.iUnion_eq_univ_iff: The union of a family of sets equals the universal set if and only if every element in the universal set belongs to at least one of the sets in the family.
explanatories.neg_lt: This theorem demonstrates that the condition of the negation of one element being less than another is equivalent to the condition of the negation of the second element being less than the first element in the context of an additive group.
explanatories.neg_le_abs: This theorem states that the negation of an element is less than or equal to its absolute value in the context of a lattice and additive group.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Nat.lt_floor_add_one: This theorem asserts that a given element in a linear ordered semiring is always less than the sum of the largest natural number not exceeding it and one.
explanatories.le_abs_self: The theorem states that any element is less than or equal to its absolute value in the context of a lattice and an additive group.

Real.finiteSpanningSetsInIooRat.fullDefinition: def finiteSpanningSetsInIooRat (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] :     μ.FiniteSpanningSetsIn (⋃ (a : ℚ) (b : ℚ) (_ : a < b), {Ioo (a : ℝ) (b : ℝ)}) where   set n := Ioo (-(n + 1)) (n + 1)   set_mem n := by     simp only [mem_iUnion, mem_singleton_iff]     refine ⟨-(n + 1 : ℕ), n + 1, ?_, by simp⟩     -- TODO: norm_cast fails here?     push_cast     exact neg_lt_self n.cast_add_one_pos   finite n := measure_Ioo_lt_top   spanning :=     iUnion_eq_univ_iff.2 fun x =>       ⟨⌊|x|⌋₊, neg_lt.1 ((neg_le_abs x).trans_lt (Nat.lt_floor_add_one _)),         (le_abs_self x).trans_lt (Nat.lt_floor_add_one _)⟩
Real.finiteSpanningSetsInIooRat.description: A locally finite measure on the real numbers has finite spanning sets consisting of open intervals with rational endpoints defined by pairs of rational numbers.

MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet.comment:
An analytic set is a set which is the continuous image of some Polish space. There are several
equivalent characterizations of this definition. For the definition, we pick one that avoids
universe issues: a set is analytic if and only if it is a continuous image of `ℕ → ℕ` (or if it
is empty). The above more usual characterization is given
in `analyticSet_iff_exists_polishSpace_range`.

Warning: these are analytic sets in the context of descriptive set theory (which is why they are
registered in the namespace `MeasureTheory`). They have nothing to do with analytic sets in the
context of complex analysis.

Measurable.measurableSet_preimage_iff_of.code:

  [StandardBorelSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Z] [CountablySeparated Z] {f : X → Z} (hf : Measurable f)
  (hsurj : Surjective f) {s : Set Z} : MeasurableSet (f ⁻¹' s) ↔ MeasurableSet s
Measurable.measurableSet_preimage_iff_of.comment:
If `f : X → Z` is a surjective Borel measurable map from a standard Borel space
to a countably separated measurable space, then the preimage of a set `s`
is measurable if and only if the set is measurable.
One implication is the definition of measurability, the other one heavily relies on `X` being a
standard Borel space.

PolishSpace.borelSchroederBernstein.fullDefinition: noncomputable def borelSchroederBernstein {f : α → β} {g : β → α} (fmeas : Measurable f)     (finj : Function.Injective f) (gmeas : Measurable g) (ginj : Function.Injective g) : α ≃ᵐ β :=   letI := upgradeStandardBorel α   letI := upgradeStandardBorel β   (fmeas.measurableEmbedding finj).schroederBernstein (gmeas.measurableEmbedding ginj)

MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteSpanningSets.fullDefinition: noncomputable def FiniteSpanningSetsIn.prod {ν : Measure β} {C : Set (Set α)} {D : Set (Set β)}     (hμ : μ.FiniteSpanningSetsIn C) (hν : ν.FiniteSpanningSetsIn D) :     (μ.prod ν).FiniteSpanningSetsIn (image2 (· ×ˢ ·) C D) := by   haveI := hν.sigmaFinite   refine     ⟨fun n => hμ.set n.unpair.1 ×ˢ hν.set n.unpair.2, fun n =>       mem_image2_of_mem (hμ.set_mem _) (hν.set_mem _), fun n => ?_, ?_⟩   · rw [prod_prod]     exact mul_lt_top (hμ.finite _).ne (hν.finite _).ne   · simp_rw [iUnion_unpair_prod, hμ.spanning, hν.spanning, univ_prod_univ]
MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteSpanningSets.description: The definition establishes that the product measure of two measures with finite spanning sets is itself associated with the rectangles formed by the Cartesian product of those finite spanning sets.

the integral of `f` is equal to the iterated integral.

MeasureTheory.piPremeasure.code:
MeasureTheory.piPremeasure.{u_1, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_3} [Fintype ι] (m : (i : ι) → OuterMeasure (α i))
  (s : Set ((i : ι) → α i)) : ℝ≥0∞
MeasureTheory.piPremeasure.comment:
An upper bound for the measure in a finite product space.
It is defined to by taking the image of the set under all projections, and taking the product
of the measures of these images.
For measurable boxes it is equal to the correct measure.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

MeasureTheory.piPremeasure.fullDefinition: def piPremeasure (m : ∀ i, OuterMeasure (α i)) (s : Set (∀ i, α i)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=   ∏ i, m i (eval i '' s)
MeasureTheory.piPremeasure.description: This definition describes a method for calculating an upper bound for the measure in a finite product space by using the measures of the images obtained through projections of the sets involved.

  (m : (i : ι) → OuterMeasure (α i)) : OuterMeasure ((i : ι) → α i)
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.pi.comment:
`OuterMeasure.pi m` is the finite product of the outer measures `{m i | i : ι}`.
It is defined to be the maximal outer measure `n` with the property that
`n (pi univ s) ≤ ∏ i, m i (s i)`, where `pi univ s` is the product of the sets
`{s i | i : ι}`.

MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteSpanningSets.fullDefinition: def FiniteSpanningSetsIn.pi {C : ∀ i, Set (Set (α i))}     (hμ : ∀ i, (μ i).FiniteSpanningSetsIn (C i)) :     (Measure.pi μ).FiniteSpanningSetsIn (pi univ '' pi univ C) := by   haveI := fun i => (hμ i).sigmaFinite   haveI := Fintype.toEncodable ι   refine ⟨fun n => Set.pi univ fun i => (hμ i).set ((@decode (ι → ℕ) _ n).iget i),     fun n => ?_, fun n => ?_, ?_⟩ <;>   -- TODO (kmill) If this let comes before the refine, while the noncomputability checker   -- correctly sees this definition is computable, the Lean VM fails to see the binding is   -- computationally irrelevant. The `noncomputable section` doesn't help because all it does   -- is insert `noncomputable` for you when necessary.   let e : ℕ → ι → ℕ := fun n => (@decode (ι → ℕ) _ n).iget   · refine mem_image_of_mem _ fun i _ => (hμ i).set_mem _   · calc       Measure.pi μ (Set.pi univ fun i => (hμ i).set (e n i)) ≤           Measure.pi μ (Set.pi univ fun i => toMeasurable (μ i) ((hμ i).set (e n i))) :=         measure_mono (pi_mono fun i _ => subset_toMeasurable _ _)       _ = ∏ i, μ i (toMeasurable (μ i) ((hμ i).set (e n i))) :=         (pi_pi_aux μ _ fun i => measurableSet_toMeasurable _ _)       _ = ∏ i, μ i ((hμ i).set (e n i)) := by simp only [measure_toMeasurable]       _ < ∞ := ENNReal.prod_lt_top fun i _ => ((hμ i).finite _).ne   · simp_rw [(surjective_decode_iget (ι → ℕ)).iUnion_comp fun x =>         Set.pi univ fun i => (hμ i).set (x i),       iUnion_univ_pi fun i => (hμ i).set, (hμ _).spanning, Set.pi_univ]

explanatories.Set.pi: The set of dependent functions can be defined for a given index set and a family of sets, where each function's values belong to the corresponding set whenever the index is part of the specified set.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Set.mem_image_of_mem: If an element belongs to a set, then its image under a function belongs to the image of that set.
explanatories.IsPiSystem.pi: This theorem states that the product of a collection of π-systems generates a π-system.
explanatories.Encodable.surjective_decode_iget: The decoding operation is surjective, meaning that for every element of the specific type, there exists a natural number that decodes to it.
explanatories.Function.Surjective.iUnion_comp: The union of sets formed by applying a function to a surjective mapping is equal to the union of the sets directly formed from the image of that function.
explanatories.Set.iUnion_univ_pi: The union of a family of sets formed by a product of a universal set and a function is equal to the product of the universal set with the unions of those sets at each index.
explanatories.Set.pi_univ: The theorem states that the product of a set with the universal set over its indices is equal to the universal set.
explanatories.IsCountablySpanning.pi: This theorem asserts that the product of collections of countably spanning sets, taken across a finite index set, also forms a countably spanning set.
explanatories.MeasurableSpace.pi: The product of measurable spaces indexed by a type forms a measurable space itself.
explanatories.Finset.univ: This definition represents the universal finite set of a type that is finitely enumerable.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_mono: If one set is a subset of another, then the measure of the first set is less than or equal to the measure of the second set for any measure that adheres to the properties of an outer measure class.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.pi: This definition describes the finite product of outer measures, determining the maximum outer measure that adheres to a specific bounding property related to the product of sets.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.pi: This definition establishes a measure for the product of finite measurable spaces by combining the measures associated with each space into a single measure for the Cartesian product of the spaces.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.pi: This defines a measure space for a product of measurable spaces indexed by a finite type, ensuring that the product space itself is also a measurable space.
explanatories.MeasurableSet.pi: The Cartesian product of measurable sets indexed by a countable set is itself measurable if each of the sets is measurable.
explanatories.Fintype.toEncodable: A finite type can be associated with an encoding structure that allows for the arbitrary choice of an ordering within it.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.pi_pi_aux: This theorem states that the measure of a Cartesian product of measurable sets, as defined through a product measure for a finite index set, equals the product of the measures of each set within that index.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteSpanningSets: This theorem states that if a measure has finite spanning sets within a specified collection of measurable sets, then that measure is sigma-finite.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.toMeasurable: This definition introduces a measurable set that contains a given set and has the same measure as that set, often referred to as the "measurable hull."
explanatories.Set.pi_mono: The theorem states that if one set of functions is included in another for all elements of a given set, then the Cartesian product over those functions will also be included in the Cartesian product of the original set with the second set of functions.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.subset_toMeasurable: This theorem asserts that any set is a subset of its measurable counterpart defined by a given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measurableSet_toMeasurable: This theorem asserts that the set obtained from a measure by making it measurable is itself a measurable set.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_toMeasurable: This theorem states that the measure of a set, when taken as measurable using a given measure, is equal to the measure of the original set.
explanatories.ENNReal.prod_lt_top: This theorem states that the product of a finite collection of non-infinite nonnegative extended real numbers is also a non-infinite number.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteSpanningSets: This theorem asserts that if a measure is finite over a collection of spanning sets, then the measure of any individual set in that collection is also finite.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.

MeasureTheory.Measure.pi.isOpenPosMeasur.fullDefinition: instance pi.isOpenPosMeasure [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (α i)] [∀ i, IsOpenPosMeasure (μ i)] :     IsOpenPosMeasure (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi μ) := by   constructor   rintro U U_open ⟨a, ha⟩   obtain ⟨s, ⟨hs, hsU⟩⟩ := isOpen_pi_iff'.1 U_open a ha   refine ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le ?_ (measure_mono hsU))   simp only [pi_pi]   rw [CanonicallyOrderedCommSemiring.prod_pos]   intro i _   apply (hs i).1.measure_pos (μ i) ⟨a i, (hs i).2⟩
MeasureTheory.Measure.pi.isOpenPosMeasur.description: This definition asserts that the product measure constructed from a collection of measures, each defined on a measurable space with open positive measure properties, also possesses the open positive measure property.

MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  (μ : Measure E) : Measure ↑(sphere 0 1)
MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere.comment:
If `μ` is an additive Haar measure on a normed space `E`,
then `μ.toSphere` is the measure on the unit sphere in `E`
such that `μ.toSphere s = FiniteDimensional.finrank ℝ E • μ (Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 • s)`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.comap: This definition introduces a measure pulled back through a function that maps measurable sets, with the condition that the image of each measurable set under this function is null-measurable.
explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element from the base type that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.restrict: This definition describes a method for limiting a measure to a specific subset, allowing for the analysis of the measure's properties exclusively within that subset.
explanatories.Set.Iio: This definition represents the set of elements that are strictly less than a given element in a preorder structure, creating a left-infinite and right-open interval.
explanatories.Set.mem_Ioi: This theorem asserts that an element is part of the interval consisting of elements strictly greater than a given element in a preorder structure if and only if it is greater than that element.
explanatories.one_pos: One is strictly greater than zero in any type that includes definitions for zero, one, and a partial order, provided that one is not equal to zero.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.fst: The definition specifies how to obtain the marginal measure on one component of a product space from a given measure defined on the entire product space.
explanatories.MeasurableSet.univ: This theorem confirms that the universal set is measurable in any measurable space.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere.fullDefinition: def toSphere (μ : Measure E) : Measure (sphere (0 : E) 1) :=   dim E • ((μ.comap (Subtype.val ∘ (homeomorphUnitSphereProd E).symm)).restrict     (univ ×ˢ Iio ⟨1, mem_Ioi.2 one_pos⟩)).fst
MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere.description: This defines a measure on the unit sphere of a normed space that is derived from an additive Haar measure on that space.

MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere.eq_1.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere.eq_1.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  (μ : Measure E) :
  μ.toSphere =
    dim E •
      ((comap (Subtype.val ∘ ⇑(homeomorphUnitSphereProd E).symm) μ).restrict (univ ×ˢ Iio ⟨1, toSphere.proof_1⟩)).fst

MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere_apply_aux.code:

MeasureTheory.toMeasurable.code: MeasureTheory.toMeasurable.{u_6} {α : Type u_6} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (s : Set α) : Set α
MeasureTheory.toMeasurable.comment:
A measurable set `t ⊇ s` such that `μ t = μ s`. It even satisfies `μ (t ∩ u) = μ (s ∩ u)` for
any measurable set `u` if `μ s ≠ ∞`, see `measure_toMeasurable_inter`.
(This property holds without the assumption `μ s ≠ ∞` when the space is s-finite -- for example
σ-finite), see `measure_toMeasurable_inter_of_sFinite`).
If `s` is a null measurable set, then
we also have `t =ᵐ[μ] s`, see `NullMeasurableSet.toMeasurable_ae_eq`.
This notion is sometimes called a "measurable hull" in the literature.

MeasureTheory.toMeasurable.description: This definition introduces a measurable set that contains a given set and has the same measure as that set, often referred to as the "measurable hull."

    if h : ∃ t ⊇ s, MeasurableSet t ∧ t =ᶠ[ae μ] s then h.choose

      else ⋯.choose

explanatories.Finset.nullMeasurableSet: This theorem asserts that any finite set is null measurable with respect to a given measure if the measurable space allows for the consideration of singleton sets as null measurable.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.toOuterMeasure: This definition describes a transformation that converts a measure defined on a measurable space into an outer measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.trimmed: This theorem asserts that for any measure defined on a measurable space, the trimmed measure is equal to the associated outer measure.

MeasureTheory.measure_limsup_eq_zero.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} {s : ℕ → Set α}
  (hs : ∑' (i : ℕ), μ (s i) ≠ ⊤) : μ (limsup s atTop) = 0
MeasureTheory.measure_limsup_eq_zero.comment:
One direction of the **Borel-Cantelli lemma** (sometimes called the "*first* Borel-Cantelli
lemma"): if (sᵢ) is a sequence of sets such that `∑ μ sᵢ` is finite, then the limit superior of the
`sᵢ` is a null set.

Note: for the *second* Borel-Cantelli lemma (applying to independent sets in a probability space),
see `ProbabilityTheory.measure_limsup_eq_one`.

MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_toMeasurab.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_toMeasurable_inter.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α}
  {s t : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : μ t ≠ ⊤) : μ (toMeasurable μ t ∩ s) = μ (t ∩ s)
MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_toMeasurab.comment:
The measurable superset `toMeasurable μ t` of `t` (which has the same measure as `t`)
satisfies, for any measurable set `s`, the equality `μ (toMeasurable μ t ∩ s) = μ (u ∩ s)`.
Here, we require that the measure of `t` is finite. The conclusion holds without this assumption
when the measure is s-finite (for example when it is σ-finite),
see `measure_toMeasurable_inter_of_sFinite`.

MeasureTheory.Measure.comapₗ.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.comapₗ.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace β] [MeasurableSpace α]
  (f : α → β) : Measure β →ₗ[ℝ≥0∞] Measure α
MeasureTheory.Measure.comapₗ.comment:
Pullback of a `Measure` as a linear map. If `f` sends each measurable set to a measurable
set, then for each measurable set `s` we have `comapₗ f μ s = μ (f '' s)`.

If the linearity is not needed, please use `comap` instead, which works for a larger class of
functions.

explanatories.MeasurableSet: This definition specifies a condition for a set to be considered measurable within a given measurable space.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.le_toOuterMeasure_caratheo: This theorem states that any measurable space is contained within the Carathéodory outer measure associated with a given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.liftLinear: This definition describes a method for converting a linear map between outer measures into a linear map between measures, ensuring that every measurable set retains the Carathéodory measurability property with respect to the transformed measure.
explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.comap: An outer measure can be transformed or pulled back through a function to define a corresponding outer measure on a different type.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.comap_apply: The application of a pullback operation on an outer measure equals the evaluation of the original measure on the image of the set transformed by a specified function.
explanatories.Set.image_inter: The image of the intersection of two sets under an injective function is equal to the intersection of the images of each set under that function.
explanatories.Set.image_diff: The image of the difference between two sets under an injective function is equal to the difference between the images of those sets.

MeasureTheory.Measure.comapₗ.fullDefinition: def comapₗ [MeasurableSpace α] (f : α → β) : Measure β →ₗ[ℝ≥0∞] Measure α :=   if hf : Injective f ∧ ∀ s, MeasurableSet s → MeasurableSet (f '' s) then     liftLinear (OuterMeasure.comap f) fun μ s hs t => by       simp only [OuterMeasure.comap_apply, image_inter hf.1, image_diff hf.1]       apply le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory       exact hf.2 s hs   else 0
MeasureTheory.Measure.comapₗ.description: This definition describes a linear transformation that allows for the adjustment of a measure on one measurable space to correspond to another measurable space through a measurable function that maps sets.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_inter_add_diff₀: This theorem asserts that for any set and a null measurable set, the measure of the intersection of the two sets plus the measure of the difference between the two sets equals the measure of the original set.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_inter_add_diff: This theorem states that for a measurable set and any set, the measure of their intersection added to the measure of the difference equals the measure of the original set.

explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.symm: A theorem asserting that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then they are also equal almost everywhere in the reverse order with respect to that filter.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.toMeasure: This definition outlines a method to derive a measure from an outer measure by ensuring that all sets within the associated σ-algebra are Carathéodory measurable.

explanatories.Set.image_diff: The image of the difference between two sets under an injective function is equal to the difference between the images of those sets.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.MeasurableEquiv.symm: The inverse of a measurable equivalence between two measurable spaces creates a new measurable equivalence.

MeasureTheory.Measure.comap.fullDefinition: def comap [MeasurableSpace α] (f : α → β) (μ : Measure β) : Measure α :=   if hf : Injective f ∧ ∀ s, MeasurableSet s → NullMeasurableSet (f '' s) μ then     (OuterMeasure.comap f μ.toOuterMeasure).toMeasure fun s hs t => by       simp only [OuterMeasure.comap_apply, image_inter hf.1, image_diff hf.1]       exact (measure_inter_add_diff₀ _ (hf.2 s hs)).symm   else 0
MeasureTheory.Measure.comap.description: This definition introduces a measure pulled back through a function that maps measurable sets, with the condition that the image of each measurable set under this function is null-measurable.

MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuo.code: MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {_m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (μ ν : Measure α) : Prop
MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuo.comment:
We say that `μ` is absolutely continuous with respect to `ν`, or that `μ` is dominated by `ν`,
if `ν(A) = 0` implies that `μ(A) = 0`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuo.fullDefinition: def AbsolutelyContinuous {_m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (μ ν : Measure α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃s : Set α⦄, ν s = 0 → μ s = 0
MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuo.description: This definition describes the condition under which one measure is said to be absolutely continuous with respect to another, meaning that if the second measure assigns zero measure to a set, then the first measure also assigns zero measure to that set.

MeasureTheory.Measure.QuasiMeasurePreser.comment:
By replacing a measurable set that is almost invariant with the `limsup` of its preimages, we
obtain a measurable set that is almost equal and strictly invariant.

(The `liminf` would work just as well.)

explanatories.Filter.map: A definition describing a transformation of a filter through a function that maps elements from one type to another.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.map: The pushforward operation transforms an outer measure associated with one type of space to an outer measure associated with another type of space by evaluating the original measure on the preimage of sets under a specified function.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.map_apply: The application of a mapped outer measure to a set is equal to the original measure applied to the preimage of that set under the mapping function.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map: This definition describes how to construct a new measure on one space from a measure on another space via a measurable function, resulting in a measure that is zero if the function is not almost everywhere measurable.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map_apply: This theorem establishes that the measure of the image of a measurable set under a measurable function is equal to the measure of the preimage of that set, reflecting a correspondence between measures in the original and image spaces.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuo: This theorem asserts that if one measure is absolutely continuous with respect to another, then the measure obtained by mapping through a measurable function retains this property of absolute continuity.

MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply.description: This theorem states that for a measurable embedding of a function, the measure of the image of a set under that function equals the measure of the preimage of the set.

explanatories.Set.inter_assoc: The intersection of three sets is associative, meaning the grouping of sets does not affect the result.
explanatories.Set.inter_comm: The intersection of two sets is commutative, meaning the order of the sets does not affect the result.
explanatories.Set.inter_diff_assoc: The difference between the intersection of two sets and a third set is equal to the intersection of the first set with the difference of the second set and the third set.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.le_toOuterMeasure_caratheo: This theorem states that any measurable space is contained within the Carathéodory outer measure associated with a given measure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.restrictₗ.fullDefinition: noncomputable def restrictₗ {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (s : Set α) : Measure α →ₗ[ℝ≥0∞] Measure α :=   liftLinear (OuterMeasure.restrict s) fun μ s' hs' t => by     suffices μ (s ∩ t) = μ (s ∩ t ∩ s') + μ ((s ∩ t) \ s') by       simpa [← Set.inter_assoc, Set.inter_comm _ s, ← inter_diff_assoc]     exact le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory _ _ hs' _
MeasureTheory.Measure.restrictₗ.description: This definition describes a process for restricting a measure to a specific set, treating it as a linear map that operates within the non-negative extended real number space.

MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteAtFilter.comment:
A measure is called finite at filter `f` if it is finite at some set `s ∈ f`.
Equivalently, it is eventually finite at `s` in `f.small_sets`.
MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteAtFilter.fullDefinition: def FiniteAtFilter {_m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : Filter α) : Prop :=   ∃ s ∈ f, μ s < ∞

MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_toMeasurab.code:

  {μ : Measure α} [SFinite μ] {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (t : Set α) : μ (toMeasurable μ t ∩ s) = μ (t ∩ s)
MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_toMeasurab.comment:
The measurable superset `toMeasurable μ t` of `t` (which has the same measure as `t`)
satisfies, for any measurable set `s`, the equality `μ (toMeasurable μ t ∩ s) = μ (t ∩ s)`.
This only holds when `μ` is s-finite -- for example for σ-finite measures. For a version without
this assumption (but requiring that `t` has finite measure), see `measure_toMeasurable_inter`.

MeasureTheory.sum.sigmaFinite.fullDefinition: instance sum.sigmaFinite {ι} [Finite ι] (μ : ι → Measure α) [∀ i, SigmaFinite (μ i)] :     SigmaFinite (sum μ) := by   cases nonempty_fintype ι   have : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (⋂ i : ι, spanningSets (μ i) n) := fun n =>     MeasurableSet.iInter fun i => measurable_spanningSets (μ i) n   refine ⟨⟨⟨fun n => ⋂ i, spanningSets (μ i) n, fun _ => trivial, fun n => ?_, ?_⟩⟩⟩   · rw [sum_apply _ (this n), tsum_fintype, ENNReal.sum_lt_top_iff]     rintro i -     exact (measure_mono <| iInter_subset _ i).trans_lt (measure_spanningSets_lt_top (μ i) n)   · rw [iUnion_iInter_of_monotone]     · simp_rw [iUnion_spanningSets, iInter_univ]     exact fun i => monotone_spanningSets (μ i)
MeasureTheory.sum.sigmaFinite.description: This definition states that if each measure in a finite index family is sigma-finite, then the sum of those measures is also sigma-finite.

MeasureTheory.Measure.finiteSpanningSets.fullDefinition: /-- A locally finite measure on a second countable topological space admits a finite spanning sequence of open sets. -/ noncomputable irreducible_def MeasureTheory.Measure.finiteSpanningSetsInOpen' [TopologicalSpace α]   [SecondCountableTopology α] {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] :   μ.FiniteSpanningSetsIn { K | IsOpen K } := by   suffices H : Nonempty (μ.FiniteSpanningSetsIn { K | IsOpen K }) from H.some   cases isEmpty_or_nonempty α   · exact       ⟨{  set := fun _ => ∅           set_mem := fun _ => by simp           finite := fun _ => by simp           spanning := by simp [eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton] }⟩   inhabit α   let S : Set (Set α) := { s | IsOpen s ∧ μ s < ∞ }   obtain ⟨T, T_count, TS, hT⟩ : ∃ T : Set (Set α), T.Countable ∧ T ⊆ S ∧ ⋃₀ T = ⋃₀ S :=     isOpen_sUnion_countable S fun s hs => hs.1   rw [μ.isTopologicalBasis_isOpen_lt_top.sUnion_eq] at hT   have T_ne : T.Nonempty := by     by_contra h'T     rw [not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.1 h'T, sUnion_empty] at hT     simpa only [← hT] using mem_univ (default : α)   obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ : ∃ f : ℕ → Set α, T = range f := T_count.exists_eq_range T_ne   have fS : ∀ n, f n ∈ S := by     intro n     apply TS     rw [hf]     exact mem_range_self n   refine     ⟨{  set := f         set_mem := fun n => (fS n).1         finite := fun n => (fS n).2         spanning := ?_ }⟩   refine eq_univ_of_forall fun x => ?_   obtain ⟨t, tT, xt⟩ : ∃ t : Set α, t ∈ range f ∧ x ∈ t := by     have : x ∈ ⋃₀ T := by simp only [hT, mem_univ]     simpa only [mem_sUnion, exists_prop, ← hf]   obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ : ∃ n : ℕ, f n = t := by simpa only using tT   exact mem_iUnion_of_mem _ xt

MeasureTheory.Measure.instSub.comment:
The measure `μ - ν` is defined to be the least measure `τ` such that `μ ≤ τ + ν`.
It is the equivalent of `(μ - ν) ⊔ 0` if `μ` and `ν` were signed measures.
Compare with `ENNReal.instSub`.
Specifically, note that if you have `α = {1,2}`, and `μ {1} = 2`, `μ {2} = 0`, and
`ν {2} = 2`, `ν {1} = 0`, then `(μ - ν) {1, 2} = 2`. However, if `μ ≤ ν`, and
`ν univ ≠ ∞`, then `(μ - ν) + ν = μ`.

MeasureTheory.Measure.trim.code: MeasureTheory.Measure.trim.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {m m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (hm : m ≤ m0) : Measure α
MeasureTheory.Measure.trim.comment:
Restriction of a measure to a sub-σ-algebra.
It is common to see a measure `μ` on a measurable space structure `m0` as being also a measure on
any `m ≤ m0`. Since measures in mathlib have to be trimmed to the measurable space, `μ` itself
cannot be a measure on `m`, hence the definition of `μ.trim hm`.

This notion is related to `OuterMeasure.trim`, see the lemma
`toOuterMeasure_trim_eq_trim_toOuterMeasure`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.toMeasure: This definition outlines a method to derive a measure from an outer measure by ensuring that all sets within the associated σ-algebra are Carathéodory measurable.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.toOuterMeasure: This definition describes a transformation that converts a measure defined on a measurable space into an outer measure.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.le_toOuterMeasure_caratheo: This theorem states that any measurable space is contained within the Carathéodory outer measure associated with a given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.trim: This definition describes a procedure for creating a modified outer measure by ignoring the values assigned to non-measurable sets while retaining the properties of the original measure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.trim.fullDefinition: def Measure.trim {m m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : @Measure α m0) (hm : m ≤ m0) : @Measure α m :=   @OuterMeasure.toMeasure α m μ.toOuterMeasure (hm.trans (le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory μ))
MeasureTheory.Measure.trim.description: This definition describes how to restrict a measure to a smaller σ-algebra within a measurable space.

MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.mk.code:
MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.mk.{u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace α] {M : Type u_4} [AddCommMonoid M]
  [TopologicalSpace M] (measureOf' : Set α → M) (empty' : measureOf' ∅ = 0)
  (not_measurable' : ∀ ⦃i : Set α⦄, ¬MeasurableSet i → measureOf' i = 0)
  (m_iUnion' :
    ∀ ⦃f : ℕ → Set α⦄,
      (∀ (i : ℕ), MeasurableSet (f i)) →
        Pairwise (Disjoint on f) → HasSum (fun i => measureOf' (f i)) (measureOf' (⋃ i, f i))) :
  VectorMeasure α M

MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.MutuallySing.comment:
Two vector measures `v` and `w` are said to be mutually singular if there exists a measurable
set `s`, such that for all `t ⊆ s`, `v t = 0` and for all `t ⊆ sᶜ`, `w t = 0`.

We note that we do not require the measurability of `t` in the definition since this makes it easier
to use. This is equivalent to the definition which requires measurability. To prove
`MutuallySingular` with the measurability condition, use
`MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.MutuallySingular.mk`.

MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.MutuallySing.fullDefinition: def MutuallySingular (v : VectorMeasure α M) (w : VectorMeasure α N) : Prop :=   ∃ s : Set α, MeasurableSet s ∧ (∀ t ⊆ s, v t = 0) ∧ ∀ t ⊆ sᶜ, w t = 0
MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.MutuallySing.description: Two vector measures are considered mutually singular if there exists a measurable set such that one measure is zero for all subsets within that set, and the other measure is zero for all subsets outside of it.

MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.trim.fullDefinition: def trim {m n : MeasurableSpace α} (v : VectorMeasure α M) (hle : m ≤ n) :     @VectorMeasure α m M _ _ :=   @VectorMeasure.mk α m M _ _     (fun i => if MeasurableSet[m] i then v i else 0)     (by dsimp only; rw [if_pos (@MeasurableSet.empty _ m), v.empty])     (fun i hi => by dsimp only; rw [if_neg hi])     (fun f hf₁ hf₂ => by       dsimp only       have hf₁' : ∀ k, MeasurableSet[n] (f k) := fun k => hle _ (hf₁ k)       convert v.m_iUnion hf₁' hf₂ using 1       · ext n         rw [if_pos (hf₁ n)]       · rw [if_pos (@MeasurableSet.iUnion _ _ m _ _ hf₁)])

MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure.toMeasureOfZ.fullDefinition: def toMeasureOfZeroLE (s : SignedMeasure α) (i : Set α) (hi₁ : MeasurableSet i) (hi₂ : 0 ≤[i] s) :     Measure α := by   refine Measure.ofMeasurable (s.toMeasureOfZeroLE' i hi₂) ?_ ?_   · simp_rw [toMeasureOfZeroLE', s.restrict_apply hi₁ MeasurableSet.empty, Set.empty_inter i,       s.empty]     rfl   · intro f hf₁ hf₂     have h₁ : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (i ∩ f n) := fun n => hi₁.inter (hf₁ n)     have h₂ : Pairwise (Disjoint on fun n : ℕ => i ∩ f n) := by       intro n m hnm       exact ((hf₂ hnm).inf_left' i).inf_right' i     simp only [toMeasureOfZeroLE', s.restrict_apply hi₁ (MeasurableSet.iUnion hf₁), Set.inter_comm,       Set.inter_iUnion, s.of_disjoint_iUnion_nat h₁ h₂, ENNReal.some_eq_coe, id]     have h : ∀ n, 0 ≤ s (i ∩ f n) := fun n =>       s.nonneg_of_zero_le_restrict (s.zero_le_restrict_subset hi₁ Set.inter_subset_left hi₂)     rw [NNReal.coe_tsum_of_nonneg h, ENNReal.coe_tsum]     · refine tsum_congr fun n => ?_       simp_rw [s.restrict_apply hi₁ (hf₁ n), Set.inter_comm]     · exact (NNReal.summable_mk h).2 (s.m_iUnion h₁ h₂).summable

MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegularWRT.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegularWRT.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} :
  {x : MeasurableSpace α} → Measure α → (Set α → Prop) → (Set α → Prop) → Prop
MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegularWRT.comment:
We say that a measure `μ` is *inner regular* with respect to predicates `p q : Set α → Prop`,
if for every `U` such that `q U` and `r < μ U`, there exists a subset `K ⊆ U` satisfying `p K`
of measure greater than `r`.

This definition is used to prove some facts about regular and weakly regular measures without

measure_theory.measure.inner_regular.comment:
We say that a measure `μ` is *inner regular* with respect to predicates `p q : Set α → Prop`,
if for every `U` such that `q U` and `r < μ U`, there exists a subset `K ⊆ U` satisfying `p K`
of measure greater than `r`.

This definition is used to prove some facts about regular and weakly regular measures without
repeating the proofs.

explanatories.HasSubset.Subset.trans: A theorem indicating that this is an alternative name for the transitive property of set inclusion.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegularWRT.tr: If a measure is inner regular with respect to two predicates and then inner regular with respect to a third predicate derived from the second, it follows that the measure is also inner regular with respect to the first and the third predicates.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.pseudoMetrizableSpacePs: This definition establishes that a pseudo-metrizable space can be equipped with a pseudo-metric that aligns with its topological structure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegularWRT.of: In a pseudo metrizable space, every open set can be approximated from within by closed sets, thereby establishing inner regularity for the measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.InnerRegularWRT.is: In a sigma-compact space, a measure is inner regular with respect to the predicates of being compact and closed.

StieltjesFunction.length_subadditive_Icc.code:
StieltjesFunction.length_subadditive_Icc_Ioo (f : StieltjesFunction) {a b : ℝ} {c d : ℕ → ℝ}
  (ss : Icc a b ⊆ ⋃ i, Ioo (c i) (d i)) : ofReal (↑f b - ↑f a) ≤ ∑' (i : ℕ), ofReal (↑f (d i) - ↑f (c i))
StieltjesFunction.length_subadditive_Icc.comment:
If a compact interval `[a, b]` is covered by a union of open interval `(c i, d i)`, then
`f b - f a ≤ ∑ f (d i) - f (c i)`. This is an auxiliary technical statement to prove the same
statement for half-open intervals, the point of the current statement being that one can use
compactness to reduce it to a finite sum, and argue by induction on the size of the covering set.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_withDensity_eq_l.code:
MeasureTheory.lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α)
  {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h_mf : Measurable f) {g : α → ℝ≥0∞} :
  Measurable g → ∫⁻ (a : α), g a ∂μ.withDensity f = ∫⁻ (a : α), (f * g) a ∂μ
MeasureTheory.lintegral_withDensity_eq_l.comment:
This is Exercise 1.2.1 from [tao2010]. It allows you to express integration of a measurable
function with respect to `(μ.withDensity f)` as an integral with respect to `μ`, called the base
measure. `μ` is often the Lebesgue measure, and in this circumstance `f` is the probability density
function, and `(μ.withDensity f)` represents any continuous random variable as a
probability measure, such as the uniform distribution between 0 and 1, the Gaussian distribution,
the exponential distribution, the Beta distribution, or the Cauchy distribution (see Section 2.4
of [wasserman2004]). Thus, this method shows how to one can calculate expectations, variances,
and other moments as a function of the probability density function.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.withDensity: This definition introduces a new measure constructed by weighting an existing measure with a non-negative, measurable function over a measurable set.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_mono: If one set is a subset of another, then the measure of the first set is less than or equal to the measure of the second set for any measure that adheres to the properties of an outer measure class.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.withDensity_apply': This theorem states that the value of a measure weighted by a non-negative measurable function over a measurable set can be expressed as the integral of that function with respect to the original measure over the same set.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.spanningSets: This definition identifies a method for generating a monotone collection of finite measure sets that together cover the entire space under a sigma-finite measure.
explanatories.trivial: The statement confirms that the proposition asserting truth is indeed valid and can be proven simply.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.setLIntegral_lt_top_of_bdd: This theorem asserts that the lower Lebesgue integral of a non-negative bounded function over a set with finite measure is also finite.
explanatories.Set.inter_subset_left: The intersection of two sets is a subset of the first set.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_spanningSets_lt_to: This theorem asserts that in a sigma-finite measure space, the measure of a specified set derived from the spanning sets is always finite.
explanatories.Set.forall_mem_image: The condition that a property holds for all images of elements from a set under a function is equivalent to saying that the property holds for the function's output applied to every element of that set.
explanatories.Set.iUnion_eq_univ_iff: The union of a family of sets equals the universal set if and only if every element in the universal set belongs to at least one of the sets in the family.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.mem_spanningSets_of_index_: This theorem states that if an element belongs to a set defined by a measure that is sigma-finite, and its spanning sets index is less than or equal to a given number, then the element is part of the spanning sets for that number.
explanatories.le_max_left: This theorem states that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.Nat.le_ceil: This theorem states that any element in a linear ordered semiring is less than or equal to the smallest natural number greater than or equal to it.

MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite.withDensity.fullDefinition: protected instance SigmaFinite.withDensity [SigmaFinite μ] (f : α → ℝ≥0) :     SigmaFinite (μ.withDensity (fun x ↦ f x)) := by   refine ⟨⟨⟨fun n ↦ spanningSets μ n ∩ f ⁻¹' (Iic n), fun _ ↦ trivial, fun n ↦ ?_, ?_⟩⟩⟩   · rw [withDensity_apply']     apply setLIntegral_lt_top_of_bddAbove     · exact ((measure_mono inter_subset_left).trans_lt (measure_spanningSets_lt_top μ n)).ne     · exact ⟨n, forall_mem_image.2 fun x hx ↦ hx.2⟩   · rw [iUnion_eq_univ_iff]     refine fun x ↦ ⟨max (spanningSetsIndex μ x) ⌈f x⌉₊, ?_, ?_⟩     exact mem_spanningSets_of_index_le _ _ (le_max_left ..)     simp [Nat.le_ceil]

explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.ofMeasurable: This definition describes the construction of a measure from a countably additive function that assigns zero to the empty set.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_empty: The measure of the empty set is stated to be zero for any measure that is defined in accordance with the properties of an outer measure class.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.lintegral_const: This theorem states that the integral of a constant non-negative function over a measurable space is equal to the product of that constant and the measure of the entire space.
explanatories.MulZeroClass.zero_mul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, demonstrating that zero acts as a left absorbing element in multiplication.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_iUnion: This theorem states that for a countable collection of mutually disjoint measurable sets, the measure of their union equals the sum of their individual measures.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.lintegral_tsum: This theorem establishes that the lower Lebesgue integral of the pointwise sum of a countable family of functions is equal to the sum of the lower Lebesgue integrals of those functions.
explanatories.Measurable.aemeasurable: This theorem establishes that if a function between two measurable spaces is measurable, then it is also almost everywhere measurable with respect to a given measure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.join.fullDefinition: def join (m : Measure (Measure α)) : Measure α :=   Measure.ofMeasurable (fun s _ => ∫⁻ μ, μ s ∂m)     (by simp only [measure_empty, lintegral_const, zero_mul])     (by       intro f hf h       simp_rw [measure_iUnion h hf]       apply lintegral_tsum       intro i; exact (measurable_coe (hf i)).aemeasurable)
MeasureTheory.Measure.join.description: This definition introduces a method to combine measures nested within a measurable space, allowing the transformation of a measure on measures into a measure on the original space.

MeasureTheory.Measure.IsEverywherePos.Is.comment:
If a compact closed set is everywhere positive with respect to a left-invariant measure on a
topological group, then it is a Gδ set. This is nontrivial, as there is no second-countability or
metrizability assumption in the statement, so a general compact closed set has no reason to be
a countable intersection of open sets.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.index.code: MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.index.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (K V : Set G) : ℕ
MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.index.comment:
The index or Haar covering number or ratio of `K` w.r.t. `V`, denoted `(K : V)`:
it is the smallest number of (left) translates of `V` that is necessary to cover `K`.
It is defined to be 0 if no finite number of translates cover `K`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.InfSet.sInf: A function that computes the infimum of a given set within a framework of ordered structures.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.index.fullDefinition: noncomputable def index (K V : Set G) : ℕ :=   sInf <| Finset.card '' { t : Finset G | K ⊆ ⋃ g ∈ t, (fun h => g * h) ⁻¹' V }
MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.index.description: The Haar index of one set with respect to another is the minimum number of translations needed to cover the first set, with a value of zero if it cannot be finitely covered.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.prehaar.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] (K₀ U : Set G) (K : Compacts G) :
  ℝ
MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.prehaar.comment:
`prehaar K₀ U K` is a weighted version of the index, defined as `(K : U)/(K₀ : U)`.
In the applications `K₀` is compact with non-empty interior, `U` is open containing `1`,
and `K` is any compact set.
The argument `K` is a (bundled) compact set, so that we can consider `prehaar K₀ U` as an
element of `haarProduct` (below).

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.prehaar.description: The pre-Haar measure of a compact set relative to another compact set and an open set is defined as the ratio of their respective Haar indices when covering the open set, with specific conditions on the sets involved.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.clPrehaar.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.clPrehaar.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] (K₀ : Set G)
  (V : OpenNhdsOf 1) : Set (Compacts G → ℝ)
MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.clPrehaar.comment:
The closure of the collection of elements of the form `prehaar K₀ U`,
for `U` open neighbourhoods of `1`, contained in `V`. The closure is taken in the space
`compacts G → ℝ`, with the topology of pointwise convergence.
We show that the intersection of all these sets is nonempty, and the Haar measure
on compact sets is defined to be an element in the closure of this intersection.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.prehaar: The pre-Haar measure of a compact set relative to another compact set and an open set is defined as the ratio of their respective Haar indices when covering the open set, with specific conditions on the sets involved.
explanatories.IsCompact.closure: This theorem asserts that in a R1 space, the closure of a compact set remains compact.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.clPrehaar.fullDefinition: def clPrehaar (K₀ : Set G) (V : OpenNhdsOf (1 : G)) : Set (Compacts G → ℝ) :=   closure <| prehaar K₀ '' { U : Set G | U ⊆ V.1 ∧ IsOpen U ∧ (1 : G) ∈ U }
MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.clPrehaar.description: The closure of the collection of pre-Haar measures taken over open neighborhoods of the identity element within a specified set corresponds to compact sets and is defined with respect to the topology of pointwise convergence.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.chaar.comment:
This is the "limit" of `prehaar K₀ U K` as `U` becomes a smaller and smaller open
neighborhood of `(1 : G)`. More precisely, it is defined to be an arbitrary element
in the intersection of all the sets `clPrehaar K₀ V` in `haarProduct K₀`.
This is roughly equal to the Haar measure on compact sets,
but it can differ slightly. We do know that
`haarMeasure K₀ (interior K) ≤ chaar K₀ K ≤ haarMeasure K₀ K`.

explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.nonempty_iInt: The intersection of the Haar product of a positive compact set and the closure of pre-Haar sets for any collection of sets is nonempty.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.chaar.fullDefinition: noncomputable def chaar (K₀ : PositiveCompacts G) (K : Compacts G) : ℝ :=   Classical.choose (nonempty_iInter_clPrehaar K₀) K
MeasureTheory.Measure.haar.chaar.description: The chaar measure is defined as the limit of the pre-Haar measure for a compact set as the neighborhood around the identity shrinks, serving as a refined approximation of the Haar measure on compact sets with specific bounds in relation to the Haar measure values.

MeasureTheory.Measure.isHaarMeasure_haar.description: The Haar measure on a positive compact set is shown to qualify as a Haar measure due to its invariance, finite mass for compact sets, and positive mass for nonempty open sets.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure_unique.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure_unique.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G]
  [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] [SecondCountableTopology G] (μ : Measure G) [SigmaFinite μ] [μ.IsMulLeftInvariant]
  (K₀ : PositiveCompacts G) : μ = μ ↑K₀ • haarMeasure K₀
MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure_unique.comment:
**Uniqueness of left-invariant measures**: In a second-countable locally compact group, any
σ-finite left-invariant measure is a scalar multiple of the Haar measure.
This is slightly weaker than assuming that `μ` is a Haar measure (in particular we don't require
`μ ≠ 0`).
See also `isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_regular`
for a statement not assuming second-countability.
MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure_unique.description: Any σ-finite left-invariant measure on a second-countable locally compact group is a scalar multiple of the Haar measure associated with positive compact sets.

parallelepiped.code: parallelepiped.{u_1, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (v : ι → E) : Set E
parallelepiped.comment: The closed parallelepiped spanned by a finite family of vectors.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

parallelepiped.fullDefinition: def parallelepiped (v : ι → E) : Set E :=   (fun t : ι → ℝ => ∑ i, t i • v i) '' Icc 0 1
parallelepiped.description: The closed parallelepiped is defined as the set of all linear combinations formed by a finite family of vectors in a given vector space.

mem_parallelepiped_iff.code:
mem_parallelepiped_iff.{u_1, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (v : ι → E)
  (x : E) : x ∈ parallelepiped v ↔ ∃ t ∈ Icc 0 1, x = ∑ i : ι, t i • v i

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

mem_parallelepiped_iff.description: An element is in the closed parallelepiped spanned by a finite family of vectors if and only if it can be expressed as a linear combination of those vectors using coefficients that lie within the interval from zero to one.

image_parallelepiped.code:
image_parallelepiped.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} {F : Type u_4} [Fintype ι] [AddCommGroup E]
  [Module ℝ E] [AddCommGroup F] [Module ℝ F] (f : E →ₗ[ℝ] F) (v : ι → E) :
  ⇑f '' parallelepiped v = parallelepiped (⇑f ∘ v)
image_parallelepiped.description: The image of the closed parallelepiped spanned by a finite family of vectors under a linear map is equal to the closed parallelepiped spanned by the images of those vectors under the same map.

parallelepiped_comp_equiv.code:
parallelepiped_comp_equiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {ι' : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι']
  [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (v : ι → E) (e : ι' ≃ ι) : parallelepiped (v ∘ ⇑e) = parallelepiped v
parallelepiped_comp_equiv.comment: Reindexing a family of vectors does not change their parallelepiped.
parallelepiped_comp_equiv.description: Reindexing a finite family of vectors does not affect the shape of the closed parallelepiped they span.

parallelepiped_orthonormalBasis_one_dim.code:
parallelepiped_orthonormalBasis_one_dim.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (b : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ ℝ) :
  parallelepiped ⇑b = Icc 0 1 ∨ parallelepiped ⇑b = Icc (-1) 0

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.

parallelepiped_orthonormalBasis_one_dim.description: The closed parallelepiped spanned by a one-dimensional orthonormal basis is either the interval from zero to one or the interval from negative one to zero.

parallelepiped_eq_sum_segment.code:
parallelepiped_eq_sum_segment.{u_1, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
  (v : ι → E) : parallelepiped v = ∑ i : ι, segment ℝ 0 (v i)
parallelepiped_eq_sum_segment.description: The closed parallelepiped spanned by a finite family of vectors is equal to the sum of the segments from the origin to each vector in that family.

convex_parallelepiped.code:
convex_parallelepiped.{u_1, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (v : ι → E) :
  Convex ℝ (parallelepiped v)

explanatories.Convex: This definition characterizes a set as convex if, for any two points within the set, the entire line segment connecting them remains within the set.

convex_parallelepiped.description: The closed parallelepiped spanned by a finite family of vectors is a convex set in the corresponding vector space.

parallelepiped_eq_convexHull.code:
parallelepiped_eq_convexHull.{u_1, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
  (v : ι → E) : parallelepiped v = (convexHull ℝ) (∑ i : ι, {0, v i})
parallelepiped_eq_convexHull.comment: A `parallelepiped` is the convex hull of its vertices
parallelepiped_eq_convexHull.description: The closed parallelepiped spanned by a finite family of vectors is equal to the convex hull of those vectors and the origin.

parallelepiped_eq_convex_hull.code:

parallelepiped_eq_convex_hull.comment: A `parallelepiped` is the convex hull of its vertices
parallelepiped_eq_convex_hull.description: The closed parallelepiped spanned by a finite family of vectors is equal to the convex hull of those vectors and the origin.

parallelepiped_single.code:
parallelepiped_single.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a : ι → ℝ) :
  (parallelepiped fun i => Pi.single i (a i)) = uIcc 0 a
parallelepiped_single.comment: The axis aligned parallelepiped over `ι → ℝ` is a cuboid.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Pi.single: This definition describes a way to create a function that assigns a specific value to one index while defaulting to zero for all other indices in the collection.
explanatories.Set.uIcc: This definition describes a set containing all elements in a lattice that lie between two specified elements, inclusive of those endpoints.

parallelepiped_single.description: The closed parallelepiped formed by a single family of values is equivalent to the interval defined from zero to those values.
