explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.Finset.univ: This definition represents the universal finite set of a type that is finitely enumerable.
explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.
explanatories.Pi.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that for any element of a collection where each element is an instance of the "zero" type, the application of the "zero" value to that element yields the "zero" value.
explanatories.Pi.one_apply: This theorem asserts that for any element of a collection where each element is an instance of the "one" type, the application of the "one" value to that element yields the "one" value.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Set.pi_univ_Icc: This theorem states that the product of the intervals between two functions' values across an index set is equal to the interval between the overall functions themselves.
explanatories.IsCompact.image: The image of a compact set under a continuous function is also compact.
explanatories.CompactIccSpace.isCompact_Icc: A closed interval in a preorder topological space is compact for any given endpoints.
explanatories.continuous_finset_sum: The product of continuous functions defined on a finite set is itself continuous in a space where multiplication is continuous.
explanatories.continuous_apply: This theorem states that if each type in a family of types has a topology, then the function that selects the component of a dependent pair based on its index is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.smul: The scalar multiplication of two continuous functions results in a continuous function.
explanatories.continuous_const: The constant function from one topological space to another is continuous.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm: The inverse of a continuous linear equivalence between two modules also forms a continuous linear equivalence between those modules.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.toHomeomorph: A continuous linear equivalence between two modules results in a homeomorphism between their corresponding topological spaces.
explanatories.Basis.equivFun_symm_apply: This theorem establishes that the inverse of the canonical linear equivalence between functions from an index set to scalars and a vector space can be represented as a linear combination of basis vectors weighted by the function values.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.interior_pi_set: This theorem states that the interior of the product of a family of sets indexed by a finite index set is equal to the product of the interiors of each individual set.
explanatories.Set.finite_univ: The universal set is finite if its elements belong to a finite type.
explanatories.Set.univ_pi_nonempty_iff: The theorem establishes that the Cartesian product of a family of non-empty sets is non-empty if and only if each individual set in the family is non-empty.
explanatories.interior_Icc: This theorem states that the interior of the closed interval from one point to another is the open interval between those two points in a densely ordered space without minimum or maximum elements.
explanatories.Set.nonempty_Ioo: This theorem states that the open interval defined by two elements in a densely ordered preorder is non-empty if and only if the first element is strictly less than the second.
explanatories.zero_lt_one: Zero is strictly less than one in any type that includes definitions for zero, one, and a partial order, provided that one is not equal to zero.
explanatories.imp_true_iff: A statement that is true implies that a true condition is equivalent to another true condition.
explanatories.Homeomorph.image_interior: This theorem asserts that the image of the interior of a set under a homeomorphism is equal to the interior of the image of that set.
explanatories.Set.image_nonempty: The image of a set under a function is non-empty if and only if the original set is non-empty.
explanatories.MeasurableEquiv.symm: The inverse of a measurable equivalence between two measurable spaces creates a new measurable equivalence.

MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_smul.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_smul.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (μ : Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : E → F) (R : ℝ) :
  ∫ (x : E), f (R • x) ∂μ = |(R ^ finrank ℝ E)⁻¹| • ∫ (x : E), f x ∂μ
MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_smul.comment:
The integral of `f (R • x)` with respect to an additive Haar measure is a multiple of the
integral of `f`. The formula we give works even when `f` is not integrable or `R = 0`
thanks to the convention that a non-integrable function has integral zero.

explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.finrank: The finite rank of a module is defined as a natural number representing its rank, which is considered to be zero when the module has infinite rank.

MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_comp_smul.description: The integral of a function evaluated at a scaled input, with respect to an additive Haar measure, is proportional to the integral of the function itself, scaled by the inverse of the absolute value of the scaling factor raised to the dimension of the space.

MeasureTheory.QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePr.code:
MeasureTheory.QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage.mulInvariantMeasure_quotient.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G]
  [MeasurableSpace G] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G] [BorelSpace G] [PolishSpace G] {Γ : Subgroup G}
  [Γ.Normal] [T2Space (G ⧸ Γ)] [SecondCountableTopology (G ⧸ Γ)] {μ : Measure (G ⧸ Γ)} (ν : Measure G)
  [ν.IsMulLeftInvariant] [hasFun : HasFundamentalDomain (↥Γ.op) G ν] [QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage ν μ] :
  μ.IsMulLeftInvariant
MeasureTheory.QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePr.comment:
If `μ` on `G ⧸ Γ` satisfies `QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage` relative to a both left- and
right-invariant measure on `G` and `Γ` is a normal subgroup, then `μ` is a left-invariant
measure.
MeasureTheory.QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePr.description: If a measure on the quotient space is equivalent to the preimage of a left- and right-invariant measure on the group, and the subgroup is normal, then the measure on the quotient space is also left-invariant.

MeasureTheory.Measure.IsMulLeftInvariant.comment:
Assume that a measure `μ` is `IsMulLeftInvariant`, that the action of `Γ` on `G` has a
measurable fundamental domain `s` with positive finite volume, and that there is a single measurable
set `V ⊆ G ⧸ Γ` along which the pullback of `μ` and `ν` agree (so the scaling is right). Then
`μ` satisfies `QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage`. The main tool of the proof is the uniqueness of
left invariant measures, if normalized by a single positive finite-measured set.

IsFundamentalDomain.QuotientMeasureEqMea.code:
IsFundamentalDomain.QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage_HaarMeasure.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [MeasurableSpace G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G] [BorelSpace G] [PolishSpace G] {Γ : Subgroup G} [Countable ↥Γ] [Γ.Normal]
  [T2Space (G ⧸ Γ)] [SecondCountableTopology (G ⧸ Γ)] {μ : Measure (G ⧸ Γ)} (ν : Measure G) [SigmaFinite ν]
  [ν.IsHaarMeasure] [ν.IsMulRightInvariant] {𝓕 : Set G} (h𝓕 : IsFundamentalDomain (↥Γ.op) 𝓕 ν) [μ.IsMulLeftInvariant]
  [SigmaFinite μ] {V : Set (G ⧸ Γ)} (hV : (interior V).Nonempty) (meas_V : MeasurableSet V)
  (hμK : μ V = ν (QuotientGroup.mk ⁻¹' V ∩ 𝓕)) (neTopV : μ V ≠ ⊤) : QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage ν μ
IsFundamentalDomain.QuotientMeasureEqMea.comment:
Given a normal subgroup `Γ` of a topological group `G` with Haar measure `μ`, which is also
right-invariant, and a finite volume fundamental domain `𝓕`, the quotient map to `G ⧸ Γ`,
properly normalized, satisfies `QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage`.

MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain.absolu.code:
MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain.absolutelyContinuous_map.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [MeasurableSpace G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalGroup G] [BorelSpace G] {μ : Measure G} {Γ : Subgroup G} {𝓕 : Set G}
  (h𝓕 : IsFundamentalDomain (↥Γ.op) 𝓕 μ) [Countable ↥Γ] [MeasurableSpace (G ⧸ Γ)] [BorelSpace (G ⧸ Γ)]
  [μ.IsMulRightInvariant] : Measure.map mk μ ≪ Measure.map mk (μ.restrict 𝓕)
MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain.absolu.comment:
Given a quotient space `G ⧸ Γ` where `Γ` is `Countable`, and the restriction,
`μ_𝓕`, of a right-invariant measure `μ` on `G` to a fundamental domain `𝓕`, a set
in the quotient which has `μ_𝓕`-measure zero, also has measure zero under the
folding of `μ` under the quotient. Note that, if `Γ` is infinite, then the folded map
will take the value `∞` on any open set in the quotient!

essSup_comp_quotientGroup_mk.code:
essSup_comp_quotientGroup_mk.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [MeasurableSpace G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [TopologicalGroup G] [BorelSpace G] {μ : Measure G} {Γ : Subgroup G} {𝓕 : Set G}
  (h𝓕 : IsFundamentalDomain (↥Γ.op) 𝓕 μ) [Countable ↥Γ] [MeasurableSpace (G ⧸ Γ)] [BorelSpace (G ⧸ Γ)]
  [μ.IsMulRightInvariant] {g : G ⧸ Γ → ℝ≥0∞} (g_ae_measurable : AEMeasurable g (Measure.map mk (μ.restrict 𝓕))) :
  essSup g (Measure.map mk (μ.restrict 𝓕)) = essSup (fun x => g ↑x) μ

of the restriction, `μ_𝓕`, of a right-invariant measure `μ` to a fundamental domain `𝓕`, is the
same as the `essSup` of `g`'s lift to the universal cover `G` with respect to `μ`.

QuotientAddGroup.integral_mul_eq_integra.code:
QuotientAddGroup.integral_mul_eq_integral_automorphize_mul.{u_1, u_2} {G' : Type u_1} [AddGroup G'] [MeasurableSpace G']
  [TopologicalSpace G'] [TopologicalAddGroup G'] [BorelSpace G'] {μ' : Measure G'} {Γ' : AddSubgroup G'} [Countable ↥Γ']
  [MeasurableSpace (G' ⧸ Γ')] [BorelSpace (G' ⧸ Γ')] {𝓕' : Set G'} {K : Type u_2} [NormedField K] [NormedSpace ℝ K]
  [μ'.IsAddRightInvariant] {f : G' → K} (f_ℒ_1 : Integrable f μ') {g : G' ⧸ Γ' → K}
  (hg : AEStronglyMeasurable g (map QuotientAddGroup.mk (μ'.restrict 𝓕')))
  (g_ℒ_infinity : essSup (fun x => ↑‖g x‖₊) (map QuotientAddGroup.mk (μ'.restrict 𝓕')) ≠ ⊤)
  (F_ae_measurable : AEStronglyMeasurable (QuotientAddGroup.automorphize f) (map QuotientAddGroup.mk (μ'.restrict 𝓕')))
  (h𝓕 : IsAddFundamentalDomain (↥Γ'.op) 𝓕' μ') :
  ∫ (x : G'), g ↑x * f x ∂μ' =
    ∫ (x : G' ⧸ Γ'), g x * QuotientAddGroup.automorphize f x ∂map QuotientAddGroup.mk (μ'.restrict 𝓕')
QuotientAddGroup.integral_mul_eq_integra.comment:
This is the **Unfolding Trick**: Given an additive subgroup `Γ'` of an additive group `G'`, the
integral of a function `f` on `G'` times the lift to `G'` of a function `g` on the quotient
`G' ⧸ Γ'` with respect to a right-invariant measure `μ` on `G'`, is equal to the integral over
the quotient of the automorphization of `f` times `g`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.HasFundamentalDomain.mk: A measurable space with a group action has a fundamental domain if there exists a set that serves as a fundamental domain under that action with respect to a specified measure.
explanatories.essSup: The definition describes the essential supremum of a function with respect to a measure as the smallest value that is greater than or equal to the function's values almost everywhere.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuo: This theorem states that a measure is absolutely continuous with respect to another measure if the measure of any measurable set that has zero measure under the second measure also has zero measure under the first measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Integrable: The definition describes a property indicating that a function is measurable and has a finite integral with respect to a specified measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable: A function is considered almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a measure if it is equal to the limit of a sequence of simple functions except on a set of measure zero.
explanatories.QuotientGroup.automorphize: The automorphization of a function defined on a group maps it to a new function by summing the values of the original function over the orbits of a given subgroup.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.restr: If a function is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a measure, then it remains almost everywhere strongly measurable when the measure is restricted to a subset.
explanatories.QuotientAddGroup.mk: This definition indicates a procedure for mapping elements of a group to their corresponding equivalence classes in the quotient group formed by a specified subgroup.
explanatories.QuotientAddGroup.automorphize: The automorphization of a function defined on an additive group transforms it into a function on the quotient of the group by a subgroup by summing the values of the function over orbits formed by the subgroup's action.
explanatories.QuotientAddGroup.integral_mul_eq_integra: The integral of the product of a function on an additive group and its lifted counterpart on the corresponding quotient is equal to the integral over the quotient of the automorphized function times the lifted function, assuming the measure is right-invariant and the subgroup is countable.

QuotientGroup.integral_mul_eq_integral_a.description: The integral of a function multiplied by the lift of another function from a quotient space equals the integral of the automorphized version of that function multiplied by the original function on the quotient.

MeasureTheory.continuous_integral_apply_.code:
MeasureTheory.continuous_integral_apply_inv_mul.{u_1, u_2} {G : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
  [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G] [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] {μ : Measure G} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {g : G → E} (hg : Continuous g) (h'g : HasCompactSupport g) :
  Continuous fun x => ∫ (y : G), g (y⁻¹ * x) ∂μ
MeasureTheory.continuous_integral_apply_.comment:
The parameterized integral `x ↦ ∫ y, g (y⁻¹ * x) ∂μ` depends continuously on `y` when `g` is a
compactly supported continuous function on a topological group `G`, and `μ` is finite on compact
sets.

explanatories.HasCompactSupport: A function has compact multiplicative support if the closure of its multiplicative support is compact, which in a T₂ space means the function is equal to one outside a compact set.

MeasureTheory.continuous_integral_apply_.description: The theorem shows that the integral of a continuous function, when parameterized by an element from a topological group, varies continuously as that element changes, provided the function has compact support and the measure is finite on compact sets.

MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeft.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeftInvariant_isMulRightInvariant_combo.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace G]
  [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G] [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] {μ ν : Measure G} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
  [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν] [μ.IsMulLeftInvariant] [ν.IsMulRightInvariant] [ν.IsOpenPosMeasure] {f g : G → ℝ}
  (hf : Continuous f) (h'f : HasCompactSupport f) (hg : Continuous g) (h'g : HasCompactSupport g) (g_nonneg : 0 ≤ g)
  {x₀ : G} (g_pos : g x₀ ≠ 0) :
  ∫ (x : G), f x ∂μ = (∫ (y : G), f y * (∫ (z : G), g (z⁻¹ * y) ∂ν)⁻¹ ∂ν) * ∫ (x : G), g x ∂μ
MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeft.comment:
In a group with a left invariant measure `μ` and a right invariant measure `ν`, one can express
integrals with respect to `μ` as integrals with respect to `ν` up to a constant scaling factor
(given in the statement as `∫ x, g x ∂μ` where `g` is a fixed reference function) and an
explicit density `y ↦ 1/∫ z, g (z⁻¹ * y) ∂ν`.

explanatories.HasCompactSupport: A function has compact multiplicative support if the closure of its multiplicative support is compact, which in a T₂ space means the function is equal to one outside a compact set.

MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeft.description: The theorem demonstrates how to relate integrals with respect to two different measures on a topological group, where one measure is left invariant and the other is right invariant, through an expression involving a fixed reference function and a density term.

MeasureTheory.Measure.exists_integral_is.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.exists_integral_isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_hasCompactSupport.{u_1} {G : Type u_1}
  [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G] [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] (μ' μ : Measure G)
  [μ.IsHaarMeasure] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ'] [μ'.IsMulLeftInvariant] :
  ∃ c, ∀ (f : G → ℝ), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → ∫ (x : G), f x ∂μ' = ∫ (x : G), f x ∂c • μ
MeasureTheory.Measure.exists_integral_is.comment:
Given two left-invariant measures which are finite on
compacts, they coincide in the following sense: they give the same value to the integral of
continuous compactly supported functions, up to a multiplicative constant.

explanatories.HasCompactSupport: A function has compact multiplicative support if the closure of its multiplicative support is compact, which in a T₂ space means the function is equal to one outside a compact set.

MeasureTheory.Measure.exists_integral_is.description: The theorem states that for two left-invariant measures that are finite on compact sets, there exists a constant such that the integrals of continuous functions with compact support are equal up to this multiplicative constant.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G]
  [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] (μ' μ : Measure G) [μ.IsHaarMeasure] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ']
  [μ'.IsMulLeftInvariant] : ℝ≥0
MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor.comment:
Given two left-invariant measures which are finite on compacts, `haarScalarFactor μ' μ` is a
scalar such that `∫ f dμ' = (haarScalarFactor μ' μ) ∫ f dμ` for any compactly supported continuous
function `f`.

Note that there is a dissymmetry in the assumptions between `μ'` and `μ`: the measure `μ'` needs
only be finite on compact sets, while `μ` has to be finite on compact sets and positive on open
sets, i.e., a Haar measure, to exclude for instance the case where `μ = 0`, where the definition
doesn't make sense.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.exists_integral_is: The theorem states that for two left-invariant measures that are finite on compact sets, there exists a constant such that the integrals of continuous functions with compact support are equal up to this multiplicative constant.
explanatories.Exists.choose: An existential statement guarantees the existence of an element satisfying a property, allowing for the extraction of such an element from the statement.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def haarScalarFactor     (μ' μ : Measure G) [IsHaarMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ'] [IsMulLeftInvariant μ'] :     ℝ≥0 :=   if ¬ LocallyCompactSpace G then 1   else (exists_integral_isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_hasCompactSupport μ' μ).choose
MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor.description: The definition establishes a non-negative scalar that relates two left-invariant measures finite on compact sets, ensuring that the integral of any compactly supported continuous function under one measure is equal to the product of this scalar and the integral under the other measure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeft.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_hasCompactSupport.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace G]
  [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G] [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] (μ' μ : Measure G) [μ.IsHaarMeasure]
  [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ'] [μ'.IsMulLeftInvariant] {f : G → ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) (h'f : HasCompactSupport f) :
  ∫ (x : G), f x ∂μ' = ∫ (x : G), f x ∂μ'.haarScalarFactor μ • μ
MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeft.comment:
Two left invariant measures integrate in the same way continuous compactly supported functions,
up to the scalar `haarScalarFactor μ' μ`. See also
`measure_isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_isCompact_closure`, which gives the same result for compact
sets, and `measure_isHaarMeasure_eq_smul_of_isOpen` for open sets.

MeasureTheory.Measure.integral_isMulLeft.description: The theorem establishes that for two left-invariant measures, the integrals of continuous functions with compact support under these measures are equal, scaled by a specific factor derived from the Haar measures.

MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor_e.code:

  [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] (μ' μ ν : Measure G) [μ.IsHaarMeasure] [ν.IsHaarMeasure]

MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor_e.description: The theorem states that the Haar scalar factor relating two left-invariant measures can be expressed as the product of their respective Haar scalar factors when one measure is scaled by the other.

MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_preimage_i.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_preimage_isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_hasCompactSupport.{u_1} {G : Type u_1}
  [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G] [TopologicalGroup G] [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] (μ' μ : Measure G)

MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_preimage_i.comment:
Two left invariant measures give the same mass to level sets of continuous compactly supported
functions, up to the scalar `haarScalarFactor μ' μ`.

Auxiliary lemma in the proof of the more general
`measure_isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_isCompact_closure`, which works for any set with
compact closure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.smul_measure_isMul.code:

explanatories.ContinuousInv.continuous_inv: The inversion operation in a topological group is continuous.
explanatories.Homeomorph.inv: The operation of taking the inverse of elements in a topological group defines a homeomorphism from the group to itself.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne': A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then the two elements cannot be equal.
explanatories.Set.image: This defines the image of a set under a function, producing a new set consisting of all values that result from applying the function to elements of the original set.
explanatories.IsCompact.image: The image of a compact set under a continuous function is also compact.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.inv: This definition constructs a new measure by associating each set with the measure of its inverse set, where the inverse set is defined pointwise.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor: The definition establishes a non-negative scalar that relates two left-invariant measures finite on compact sets, ensuring that the integral of any compactly supported continuous function under one measure is equal to the product of this scalar and the integral under the other measure.
explanatories.smul_smul: This theorem shows that the action of the product of two elements from a monoid on another element is the same as performing the actions sequentially and is associative.
explanatories.IsCompact.measure_lt_top: This theorem states that if a measure is finite on compact sets, then any compact subset of the space must have finite measure.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.
explanatories.IsClosed.isCompact: A closed subset of a compact space is also compact.
explanatories.IsClosed.inv: The inverse of a closed set in a topological group is also closed.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.isMulLeftInvariant: The theorem establishes that for two regular, finite left-invariant measures on a locally compact group, the measures are equal up to a scalar factor related to the Haar measures.
explanatories.Classical.arbitrary: A nonempty type can be represented by an arbitrary element chosen from it.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map: This definition describes how to construct a new measure on one space from a measure on another space via a measurable function, resulting in a measure that is zero if the function is not almost everywhere measurable.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map_smul: This theorem states that applying a measurable function to a scaled measure results in the same scaling applied to the measure of the image under that function.
explanatories.pow_two: This theorem states that in a monoid, the square of an element is equal to the element multiplied by itself.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map_map: This theorem states that mapping a measure through two measurable functions in succession is equivalent to mapping the measure through the composition of those two functions.
explanatories.Continuous.measurable: A continuous function from a space with an open measurable structure to a Borel space is guaranteed to be measurable.
explanatories.inv_involutive: The inverse operation in an involutive structure is its own inverse, meaning applying it twice returns the original element.
explanatories.Function.Involutive.comp_self: An involutive function, when applied twice, results in the identity function.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map_id: This theorem states that applying the identity mapping to a measure results in the same measure.
explanatories.ENNReal.mul_eq_mul_right: This theorem asserts that for two equal products involving a non-zero, finite extended nonnegative real number, the equality of the original numbers follows from the equality of their products with that number.

MeasureTheory.Measure.IsHaarMeasure.isIn.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) IsHaarMeasure.isInvInvariant_of_regular     [LocallyCompactSpace G] [Regular μ] : IsInvInvariant μ := by   -- the image measure is a Haar measure. By uniqueness up to multiplication, it is of the form   -- `c μ`. Applying again inversion, one gets the measure `c^2 μ`. But since inversion is an   -- involution, this is also `μ`. Hence, `c^2 = 1`, which implies `c = 1`.   constructor   let c : ℝ≥0∞ := haarScalarFactor μ.inv μ   have hc : μ.inv = c • μ := isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_regular μ.inv μ   have : map Inv.inv (map Inv.inv μ) = c ^ 2 • μ := by     rw [← inv_def μ, hc, Measure.map_smul, ← inv_def μ, hc, smul_smul, pow_two]   have μeq : μ = c ^ 2 • μ := by     rw [map_map continuous_inv.measurable continuous_inv.measurable] at this     simpa only [inv_involutive, Involutive.comp_self, Measure.map_id]   have K : PositiveCompacts G := Classical.arbitrary _   have : c ^ 2 * μ K = 1 ^ 2 * μ K := by     conv_rhs => rw [μeq]     simp   have : c ^ 2 = 1 ^ 2 :=     (ENNReal.mul_eq_mul_right (measure_pos_of_nonempty_interior _ K.interior_nonempty).ne'           K.isCompact.measure_lt_top.ne).1 this   have : c = 1 := (ENNReal.pow_strictMono two_ne_zero).injective this   rw [hc, this, one_smul]
MeasureTheory.Measure.IsHaarMeasure.isIn.description: Any regular Haar measure on an abelian group is invariant under the operation of taking inverses.

explanatories.TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts.interi: This theorem asserts that the interior of a positive compact set in a topological space is non-empty.
explanatories.TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts.isComp: This theorem states that a positive compact set in a topological space is compact.
explanatories.ENNReal.pow_strictMono: This theorem establishes that the function which raises a variable to a positive integer power is strictly monotonic, meaning it consistently increases without flat intervals.
explanatories.two_ne_zero: This theorem asserts that the number two is not equal to zero in any type that permits both zero and the natural representation of two, assuming two is non-zero.

explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.

MeasureTheory.Measure.IsAddHaarMeasure.i.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) IsHaarMeasure.isInvInvariant_of_regular     [LocallyCompactSpace G] [Regular μ] : IsInvInvariant μ := by   -- the image measure is a Haar measure. By uniqueness up to multiplication, it is of the form   -- `c μ`. Applying again inversion, one gets the measure `c^2 μ`. But since inversion is an   -- involution, this is also `μ`. Hence, `c^2 = 1`, which implies `c = 1`.   constructor   let c : ℝ≥0∞ := haarScalarFactor μ.inv μ   have hc : μ.inv = c • μ := isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_regular μ.inv μ   have : map Inv.inv (map Inv.inv μ) = c ^ 2 • μ := by     rw [← inv_def μ, hc, Measure.map_smul, ← inv_def μ, hc, smul_smul, pow_two]   have μeq : μ = c ^ 2 • μ := by     rw [map_map continuous_inv.measurable continuous_inv.measurable] at this     simpa only [inv_involutive, Involutive.comp_self, Measure.map_id]   have K : PositiveCompacts G := Classical.arbitrary _   have : c ^ 2 * μ K = 1 ^ 2 * μ K := by     conv_rhs => rw [μeq]     simp   have : c ^ 2 = 1 ^ 2 :=     (ENNReal.mul_eq_mul_right (measure_pos_of_nonempty_interior _ K.interior_nonempty).ne'           K.isCompact.measure_lt_top.ne).1 this   have : c = 1 := (ENNReal.pow_strictMono two_ne_zero).injective this   rw [hc, this, one_smul]
MeasureTheory.Measure.IsAddHaarMeasure.i.description: Any regular Haar measure on an abelian group is invariant under the operation of taking inverses.

MeasureTheory.Measure.isMulLeftInvariant.code:
MeasureTheory.Measure.isMulLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_innerRegular.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G]
  [TopologicalGroup G] [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] [LocallyCompactSpace G] (μ' μ : Measure G) [μ.IsHaarMeasure]
  [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ'] [μ'.IsMulLeftInvariant] [μ.InnerRegular] [μ'.InnerRegular] :

MeasureTheory.Measure.isMulLeftInvariant.comment:
**Uniqueness of left-invariant measures**:
Given two left-invariant measures which are finite
on compacts and inner regular, they coincide up to a multiplicative constant.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.haarScalarFactor: The definition establishes a non-negative scalar that relates two left-invariant measures finite on compact sets, ensuring that the integral of any compactly supported continuous function under one measure is equal to the product of this scalar and the integral under the other measure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.isMulLeftInvariant.description: The theorem states that two finite inner regular left-invariant measures on a locally compact group are equal up to a scalar factor determined by their Haar measures.

LinearMap.exists_map_addHaar_eq_smul_addHaar'.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] (L : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)
  (μ : Measure E) (ν : Measure F) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] [ν.IsAddHaarMeasure] [LocallyCompactSpace E]

LinearMap.exists_map_addHaar_eq_smul_add.comment:
The image of an additive Haar measure under a surjective linear map is proportional to a given
additive Haar measure. The proportionality factor will be infinite if the linear map has a
nontrivial kernel.

explanatories.Function.Surjective: This definition identifies a function as surjective if every element in the output set can be achieved by applying the function to at least one element from the input set.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map: This definition describes how to construct a new measure on one space from a measure on another space via a measurable function, resulting in a measure that is zero if the function is not almost everywhere measurable.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar: The Haar measure is a specific type of measure defined on locally compact groups that allows for the integration and analysis of functions over these groups.

LinearMap.exists_map_addHaar_eq_smul_add.description: The image of an additive Haar measure on one space under a surjective linear map is shown to be proportional to an additive Haar measure on another space, with a positive finite scaling factor, unless the linear map has a nontrivial kernel.

LinearMap.exists_map_addHaar_eq_smul_add.description: The image of an additive Haar measure on one space under a surjective linear map is proportional to another additive Haar measure on a different space, with a positive scaling factor that may be infinite.

MeasureTheory.ae_comp_linearMap_mem_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] (L : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)
  (μ : Measure E) (ν : Measure F) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] [ν.IsAddHaarMeasure] [LocallyCompactSpace E]
  (h : Function.Surjective ⇑L) {s : Set F} (hs : MeasurableSet s) : (∀ᵐ (x : E) ∂μ, L x ∈ s) ↔ ∀ᵐ (y : F) ∂ν, y ∈ s
MeasureTheory.ae_comp_linearMap_mem_iff.comment:
Given a surjective linear map `L`, it is equivalent to require a property almost everywhere
in the source or the target spaces of `L`, with respect to additive Haar measures there.

MeasureTheory.ae_comp_linearMap_mem_iff.description: The equivalence of almost everywhere properties in two spaces under a surjective linear map, with respect to their additive Haar measures, is established.

MeasureTheory.ae_ae_add_linearMap_mem_if.code:
MeasureTheory.ae_ae_add_linearMap_mem_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] (L : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)
  (μ : Measure E) (ν : Measure F) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] [ν.IsAddHaarMeasure] [LocallyCompactSpace E]
  [LocallyCompactSpace F] {s : Set F} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
  (∀ᵐ (y : F) ∂ν, ∀ᵐ (x : E) ∂μ, y + L x ∈ s) ↔ ∀ᵐ (y : F) ∂ν, y ∈ s
MeasureTheory.ae_ae_add_linearMap_mem_if.comment:
Given a linear map `L : E → F`, a property holds almost everywhere in `F` if and only if,
almost everywhere in `F`, it holds almost everywhere along the subspace spanned by the
image of `L`. This is an instance of a disintegration argument for additive Haar measures.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.MeasurableSet: This definition specifies a condition for a set to be considered measurable within a given measurable space.

MeasureTheory.ae_ae_add_linearMap_mem_if.description: A property in the target space holds almost everywhere if and only if, almost everywhere in the same space, it also holds almost everywhere along the subspace spanned by the image of a given linear map.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.comment:
We say that an outer measure `μ` in an (e)metric space is *metric* if `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t`
for any two metric separated sets `s`, `t`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.IsMetricSeparated: Two sets in an extended metric space are considered metric separated if there is a positive lower bound on the distance between any point in one set and any point in the other set.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.fullDefinition: def IsMetric (μ : OuterMeasure X) : Prop :=   ∀ s t : Set X, IsMetricSeparated s t → μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.description: An outer measure in an (e)metric space is considered metric if it satisfies the additive property for the measures of disjoint sets.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mkMetric'.pre.comment:
Auxiliary definition for `OuterMeasure.mkMetric'`: given a function on sets
`m : Set X → ℝ≥0∞`, returns the maximal outer measure `μ` such that `μ s ≤ m s`
for any set `s` of diameter at most `r`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.boundedBy: This definition establishes a unique maximal outer measure that is less than or equal to any given function assigning measures to sets, without the requirement that the measure of the empty set is zero.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.extend: This definition describes a method for extending a function that assigns non-negative extended real numbers to a specific subclass of objects, by assigning infinity to objects not included in that subclass.
explanatories.EMetric.diam: The diameter of a set in a pseudo-metric space is defined as the greatest distance between any two points in that set.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mkMetric'.pre.fullDefinition: def mkMetric'.pre (m : Set X → ℝ≥0∞) (r : ℝ≥0∞) : OuterMeasure X :=   boundedBy <| extend fun s (_ : diam s ≤ r) => m s
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mkMetric'.pre.description: This defines an outer measure that is the largest possible measure consistent with a given function on sets for those sets within a specified diameter.

If a sequence of bounded continuous non-negative functions are uniformly bounded by a constant
and tend pointwise to a limit, then their integrals (`MeasureTheory.lintegral`) against the finite
measure tend to the integral of the limit.

A related result with more general assumptions is
`MeasureTheory.tendsto_lintegral_nn_filter_of_le_const`.

MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.tendsto_test.comment:
A bounded convergence theorem for a finite measure:
If bounded continuous non-negative functions are uniformly bounded by a constant and tend to a
limit, then their integrals against the finite measure tend to the integral of the limit.
This formulation assumes:
 * the functions tend to a limit along a countably generated filter;
 * the limit is in the almost everywhere sense;
 * boundedness holds almost everywhere;
 * integration is the pairing against non-negative continuous test functions
   (`MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN`).

A related result using `MeasureTheory.lintegral` for integration is
`MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.tendsto_lintegral_nn_filter_of_le_const`.

MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.tendsto_map_.comment:
If `f : X → Y` is continuous and `Y` is equipped with the Borel sigma algebra, then
(weak) convergence of `FiniteMeasure`s on `X` implies (weak) convergence of the push-forwards
of these measures by `f`.

MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.tendsto_map_.description: This theorem proves that if a continuous function maps a sequence of finite measures converging weakly to another finite measure, then the push-forwards of these measures under the function also converge weakly.

MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.continuous_m.comment:

the push-forward of finite measures `f* : FiniteMeasure X → FiniteMeasure Y` is continuous
(in the topologies of weak convergence of measures).

MeasureTheory.Measure.withDensityᵥ.comment:
Given a measure `μ` and an integrable function `f`, `μ.withDensityᵥ f` is
the vector measure which maps the set `s` to `∫ₛ f ∂μ`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Integrable: The definition describes a property indicating that a function is measurable and has a finite integral with respect to a specified measure.
explanatories.MeasurableSet: This definition specifies a condition for a set to be considered measurable within a given measurable space.
explanatories.if_neg: If a condition is proven to be false, then the result of a conditional expression will yield the alternative value.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.hasSum_integral_iUnion: This theorem establishes that if a countable collection of disjoint measurable sets has a function that is integrable over their union, then the sum of the integrals of that function over each individual set equals the integral of the function over the entire union.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Integrable.integrableOn: This theorem asserts that if a function is integrable with respect to a measure, then it is also integrable on any subset with respect to that measure.
explanatories.if_pos: If a condition is true, then the result of a conditional expression evaluating that condition will equal the first option.
explanatories.MeasurableSet.iUnion: This theorem establishes that the union of countably many measurable sets is also measurable in a given measurable space.

MeasureTheory.Measure.withDensityᵥ.fullDefinition: def Measure.withDensityᵥ {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α → E) : VectorMeasure α E :=   if hf : Integrable f μ then     { measureOf' := fun s => if MeasurableSet s then ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ else 0       empty' := by simp       not_measurable' := fun s hs => if_neg hs       m_iUnion' := fun s hs₁ hs₂ => by         dsimp only         convert hasSum_integral_iUnion hs₁ hs₂ hf.integrableOn with n         · rw [if_pos (hs₁ n)]         · rw [if_pos (MeasurableSet.iUnion hs₁)] }   else 0
MeasureTheory.Measure.withDensityᵥ.description: Given a measure and an integrable function, the defined vector measure maps a set to the integral of the function over that set with respect to the measure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.withDensityᵥ.eq_1.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {m : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α → E) :

      { measureOf' := fun s => if MeasurableSet s then ∫ (x : α) in s, f x ∂μ else 0, empty' := ⋯, not_measurable' := ⋯,

measure_theory.finite_measure.normalize.fullDefinition: def normalize : ProbabilityMeasure Ω :=   if zero : μ.mass = 0 then ⟨Measure.dirac ‹Nonempty Ω›.some, Measure.dirac.isProbabilityMeasure⟩   else     { val := ↑(μ.mass⁻¹ • μ)       property := by         refine ⟨?_⟩         -- Porting note: paying the price that this isn't `simp` lemma now.         rw [FiniteMeasure.toMeasure_smul]         simp only [Measure.coe_smul, Pi.smul_apply, Measure.nnreal_smul_coe_apply, ne_eq,           mass_zero_iff, ENNReal.coe_inv zero, ennreal_mass]         rw [← Ne, ← ENNReal.coe_ne_zero, ennreal_mass] at zero         exact ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel zero μ.prop.measure_univ_lt_top.ne }

MeasureTheory.limsup_measure_closed_le_i.code:
MeasureTheory.limsup_measure_closed_le_iff_liminf_measure_open_ge.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  [TopologicalSpace Ω] [OpensMeasurableSpace Ω] {ι : Type u_2} {L : Filter ι} {μ : Measure Ω} {μs : ι → Measure Ω}
  [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [∀ (i : ι), IsProbabilityMeasure (μs i)] :
  (∀ (F : Set Ω), IsClosed F → limsup (fun i => (μs i) F) L ≤ μ F) ↔
    ∀ (G : Set Ω), IsOpen G → μ G ≤ liminf (fun i => (μs i) G) L
MeasureTheory.limsup_measure_closed_le_i.comment:
One pair of implications of the portmanteau theorem:
For a sequence of Borel probability measures, the following two are equivalent:

(C) The limsup of the measures of any closed set is at most the measure of the closed set
under a candidate limit measure.

(O) The liminf of the measures of any open set is at least the measure of the open set
under a candidate limit measure.

MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto.comment:
One implication of the portmanteau theorem:
Weak convergence of probability measures implies that if the boundary of a Borel set
carries no probability mass under the limit measure, then the limit of the measures of the set
equals the measure of the set under the limit probability measure.

A version with coercions to ordinary `ℝ≥0∞`-valued measures is
`MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_measure_of_null_frontier_of_tendsto'`.

  (h0 : Tendsto (fun k => μ ((⋃ n, s n) \ s k)) l (𝓝 0)) : μ (⋃ n, s n) = ⨆ n, μ (s n)
MeasureTheory.measure_iUnion_of_tendsto_.comment:
Let `μ` be an (outer) measure; let `s : ι → Set α` be a sequence of sets, `S = ⋃ n, s n`.
If `μ (S \ s n)` tends to zero along some nontrivial filter (usually `Filter.atTop` on `ι = ℕ`),
then `μ S = ⨆ n, μ (s n)`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.empty: The measure of a set is defined through an outer measure function, which assigns non-negative extended real values to subsets of a given type.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mono: The measure of a set is defined through an outer measure function, which assigns non-negative extended real values to subsets of a given type.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_iUnion_le: The measure of the union of a countable collection of sets is less than or equal to the sum of the measures of each individual set for any measure that follows the properties of an outer measure class.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Set.image_subset: The image of a subset under a function is contained within the image of the superset.
explanatories.Set.image_iUnion: The image of the union of a collection of sets under a function is equal to the union of the images of each set in the collection.

measure_theory.outer_measure.comap.fullDefinition: def comap {β} (f : α → β) : OuterMeasure β →ₗ[ℝ≥0∞] OuterMeasure α where   toFun m :=     { measureOf := fun s => m (f '' s)       empty := by simp       mono := fun {s t} h => m.mono <| image_subset f h       iUnion_nat := fun s _ => by simpa only [image_iUnion] using measure_iUnion_le _ }   map_add' m₁ m₂ := rfl   map_smul' c m := rfl

MeasureTheory.ae.comment: The “almost everywhere” filter of co-null sets.

explanatories.Filter.ofCountableUnion: A filter is constructed using a countable union property, meaning that a set belongs to this filter if its complement meets a specific inclusion criterion for countably many sets.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_sUnion_null_iff: The measure of the union of a countable collection of sets is zero if and only if the measure of each individual set in the collection is zero for any measure defined within the framework of an outer measure class.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.measure_mono_null: If one set is a subset of another and the measure of the larger set is zero, then the measure of the smaller set must also be zero for any measure that follows the properties of an outer measure class.

MeasureTheory.ae.fullDefinition: def ae (μ : F) : Filter α :=   .ofCountableUnion (μ · = 0) (fun _S hSc ↦ (measure_sUnion_null_iff hSc).2) fun _t ht _s hs ↦     measure_mono_null hs ht
MeasureTheory.ae.description: The "almost everywhere" filter represents the collection of sets that differ from a given set by at most a collection of co-null sets.

MeasureTheory.«term_=ᵐ[_]_».comment:
`f =ᵐ[μ] g` means `f` and `g` are eventually equal along the a.e. filter,
i.e. `f=g` away from a null set.

This is notation for `Filter.EventuallyEq (MeasureTheory.ae μ) f g`.
MeasureTheory.«term_=ᵐ[_]_».fullDefinition: /- Copyright (c) 2018 Mario Carneiro. All rights reserved. Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE. Authors: Mario Carneiro, Yury Kudryashov -/ import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.Basic
MeasureTheory.«term_=ᵐ[_]_».description: This definition introduces notation indicating that two functions are eventually equal with respect to a measure, meaning they are equal except on a set of measure zero.

MeasureTheory.«term_≤ᵐ[_]_».comment:
`f ≤ᵐ[μ] g` means `f` is eventually less than `g` along the a.e. filter,
i.e. `f ≤ g` away from a null set.

This is notation for `Filter.EventuallyLE (MeasureTheory.ae μ) f g`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.le_antisymm: This theorem establishes that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.iInf_le_of_le: This theorem asserts that the infimum of a family of elements is less than or equal to a given value if at least one element from that family does not exceed the same value in a complete lattice.
explanatories.Set.empty_subset: The empty set is a subset of any set.
explanatories.zero_le: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, any element is greater than or equal to zero.
explanatories.iInf_mono: This theorem establishes that if one function is pointwise less than or equal to another across a collection of indices, then the infimum of the first function is less than or equal to the infimum of the second function in a complete lattice.
explanatories.iInf_mono': This theorem establishes that if every element of one function is less than or equal to some element of another function, then the infimum of the first function is less than or equal to the infimum of the second function.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.HasSubset.Subset.trans: A theorem indicating that this is an alternative name for the transitive property of set inclusion.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add: This theorem states that if a certain condition holds for all positive real numbers and maintains a bound related to extended nonnegative real numbers, then one extended nonnegative real number is less than or equal to another.
explanatories.ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable: For any positive non-zero value, a countable collection of positive values can be found such that their sum is less than that value.
explanatories.ENNReal.coe_pos: This theorem states that a real number embedded in the extended nonnegative real numbers is positive if and only if the original real number is positive.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne': A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then the two elements cannot be equal.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.add_le_add_left: This theorem asserts that if an addition operation preserves an order relation, then adding a common element to both sides of an inequality maintains that inequality.
explanatories.le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that if one element is strictly less than another in a preorder, then it is also less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.ENNReal.tsum_add: This theorem shows that the sum of the addition of two functions evaluated at each element is equal to the sum of the first function plus the sum of the second function across the same domain.
explanatories.ENNReal.lt_add_right: This theorem asserts that for a non-infinite nonnegative extended real number added to a positive nonnegative extended real number, the sum will always be greater than the original number.
explanatories.ne_top_of_le_ne_top: In a partially ordered type with a maximum element, if an element is less than or equal to another element that is not equal to the maximum, then it must also not be equal to the maximum.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.
explanatories.ENNReal.le_tsum: This theorem establishes that the value of a non-negative extended real function at a specific point is less than or equal to the total sum of the function's values over all inputs.
explanatories.iInf_lt_iff: This theorem states that the infimum of a function is less than a given value if and only if there exists at least one input for which the function's value is less than that same value in a complete linear order.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.le_iInf: This theorem demonstrates that if an element is less than or equal to all elements produced by a function mapping from an index set, then it is also less than or equal to the infimum of those function values in a complete lattice.
explanatories.ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum: This theorem states that if one collection of non-negative extended real functions is pointwise less than or equal to another, then the sum of the first collection is less than or equal to the sum of the second collection.
explanatories.ENNReal.tsum_prod: This theorem states that the total sum of a function defined on pairs of elements from two types is equal to the total sum obtained by summing over each type individually.
explanatories.Equiv.tsum_eq: The total sum of a function over a set with a bijective mapping is equal to the total sum of the original function over the mapped set.
explanatories.iInf_le: This theorem asserts that the infimum of a function over an index set is always less than or equal to the function's value at any specific index from that set.
explanatories.Set.iUnion_subset: If every set in a family of sets is contained within another set, then the union of all those sets is also contained within that same set.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.ofFunction.fullDefinition: protected def ofFunction : OuterMeasure α :=   let μ s := ⨅ (f : ℕ → Set α) (_ : s ⊆ ⋃ i, f i), ∑' i, m (f i)   { measureOf := μ     empty :=       le_antisymm         ((iInf_le_of_le fun _ => ∅) <| iInf_le_of_le (empty_subset _) <| by simp [m_empty])         (zero_le _)     mono := fun {s₁ s₂} hs => iInf_mono fun f => iInf_mono' fun hb => ⟨hs.trans hb, le_rfl⟩     iUnion_nat := fun s _ =>       ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add <| by         intro ε hε (hb : (∑' i, μ (s i)) < ∞)         rcases ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable (ENNReal.coe_pos.2 hε).ne' ℕ with ⟨ε', hε', hl⟩         refine le_trans ?_ (add_le_add_left (le_of_lt hl) _)         rw [← ENNReal.tsum_add]         choose f hf using           show ∀ i, ∃ f : ℕ → Set α, (s i ⊆ ⋃ i, f i) ∧ (∑' i, m (f i)) < μ (s i) + ε' i by             intro i             have : μ (s i) < μ (s i) + ε' i :=               ENNReal.lt_add_right (ne_top_of_le_ne_top hb.ne <| ENNReal.le_tsum _)                 (by simpa using (hε' i).ne')             rcases iInf_lt_iff.mp this with ⟨t, ht⟩             exists t             contrapose! ht             exact le_iInf ht         refine le_trans ?_ (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun i => le_of_lt (hf i).2)         rw [← ENNReal.tsum_prod, ← Nat.pairEquiv.symm.tsum_eq]         refine iInf_le_of_le _ (iInf_le _ ?_)         apply iUnion_subset         intro i         apply Subset.trans (hf i).1         apply iUnion_subset         simp only [Nat.pairEquiv_symm_apply]         rw [iUnion_unpair]         intro j         apply subset_iUnion₂ i }
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.ofFunction.description: This definition states that for any function assigning measures to sets and satisfying the condition that the measure of the empty set is zero, there exists a unique maximal outer measure that is less than or equal to that function for all sets.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.ofFunction_un.code:
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.ofFunction_union_of_top_of_nonempty_inter.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} {m : Set α → ℝ≥0∞}
  {m_empty : m ∅ = 0} {s t : Set α} (h : ∀ (u : Set α), (s ∩ u).Nonempty → (t ∩ u).Nonempty → m u = ⊤) :
  (OuterMeasure.ofFunction m m_empty) (s ∪ t) =
    (OuterMeasure.ofFunction m m_empty) s + (OuterMeasure.ofFunction m m_empty) t
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.ofFunction_un.comment:
If `m u = ∞` for any set `u` that has nonempty intersection both with `s` and `t`, then
`μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t`, where `μ = MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.ofFunction m m_empty`.

E.g., if `α` is an (e)metric space and `m u = ∞` on any set of diameter `≥ r`, then this lemma
implies that `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t` on any two sets such that `r ≤ edist x y` for all `x ∈ s`
and `y ∈ t`.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.boundedBy_uni.comment:
If `m u = ∞` for any set `u` that has nonempty intersection both with `s` and `t`, then
`μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t`, where `μ = MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.boundedBy m`.

E.g., if `α` is an (e)metric space and `m u = ∞` on any set of diameter `≥ r`, then this lemma
implies that `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t` on any two sets such that `r ≤ edist x y` for all `x ∈ s`
and `y ∈ t`.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.sInfGen.comment:
Given a set of outer measures, we define a new function that on a set `s` is defined to be the
infimum of `μ(s)` for the outer measures `μ` in the collection. We ensure that this
function is defined to be `0` on `∅`, even if the collection of outer measures is empty.
The outer measure generated by this function is the infimum of the given outer measures.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.sInfGen.fullDefinition: def sInfGen (m : Set (OuterMeasure α)) (s : Set α) : ℝ≥0∞ :=   ⨅ (μ : OuterMeasure α) (_ : μ ∈ m), μ s
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.sInfGen.description: This definition establishes a function that calculates the infimum of a set of outer measures on a given set, with the provision that it evaluates to zero for empty sets regardless of the input collection.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsCaratheodor.comment:
A set `s` is Carathéodory-measurable for an outer measure `m` if for all sets `t` we have
`m t = m (t ∩ s) + m (t \ s)`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsCaratheodor.fullDefinition: def IsCaratheodory (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ t, m t = m (t ∩ s) + m (t \ s)
MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsCaratheodor.description: A set is considered Carathéodory-measurable with respect to an outer measure if the measure of any set is equal to the sum of the measures of its intersection with the set and its complement relative to the set.

MeasureTheory.inducedOuterMeasure.comment:
Given an arbitrary function on a subset of sets, we can define the outer measure corresponding
to it (this is the unique maximal outer measure that is at most `m` on the domain of `m`).

explanatories.MeasureTheory.extend_empty: This theorem establishes that if a function assigns a value of zero to the empty set in its subclass and the subclass conditions hold for the empty set, then the extension of that function to the empty set also equals zero.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.ofFunction: This definition states that for any function assigning measures to sets and satisfying the condition that the measure of the empty set is zero, there exists a unique maximal outer measure that is less than or equal to that function for all sets.

MeasureTheory.inducedOuterMeasure.fullDefinition: def inducedOuterMeasure : OuterMeasure α :=   OuterMeasure.ofFunction (extend m) (extend_empty P0 m0)
MeasureTheory.inducedOuterMeasure.description: This definition introduces an outer measure that corresponds to a given function defined on a subset of sets, ensuring it is the unique maximal outer measure that does not exceed the function's values on its domain.

MeasureTheory.inducedOuterMeasure_union_.comment:
If `P u` is `False` for any set `u` that has nonempty intersection both with `s` and `t`, then
`μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t`, where `μ = inducedOuterMeasure m P0 m0`.

E.g., if `α` is an (e)metric space and `P u = diam u < r`, then this lemma implies that
`μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t` on any two sets such that `r ≤ edist x y` for all `x ∈ s` and `y ∈ t`.

  {P0 : P ∅} {m0 : m ∅ P0 = 0} (PU : ∀ ⦃f : ℕ → Set α⦄, (∀ (i : ℕ), P (f i)) → P (⋃ i, f i))
  (msU : ∀ ⦃f : ℕ → Set α⦄ (hm : ∀ (i : ℕ), P (f i)), m (⋃ i, f i) ⋯ ≤ ∑' (i : ℕ), m (f i) ⋯)

  MeasurableSet s ↔
    ∀ (t : Set α),
      P t →
        (inducedOuterMeasure m P0 m0) (t ∩ s) + (inducedOuterMeasure m P0 m0) (t \ s) ≤ (inducedOuterMeasure m P0 m0) t

of `s`.

aeSeqSet.comment:

whose complement has measure 0 such that for all `x ∈ aeSeqSet`, `f i x` is equal to

Measurable.inner.code:
Measurable.inner.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E]

  ∀ {x : MeasurableSpace α} [inst : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_1 : OpensMeasurableSpace E]

explanatories.Measurable.pow: This theorem asserts that the function which raises the value of one measurable function to the power determined by another measurable function is also measurable in a specified measurable space.
explanatories.ENNReal.measurable_of_measurable_nnreal_: If a function defined on the product of non-negative extended reals and another measurable space is measurable when one argument is a variable from the non-negative extended reals and the other is from the second space, and is also measurable when the first argument is fixed at positive infinity, then the function is measurable overall.
explanatories.ENNReal.coe_rpow_def: The theorem defines that the exponentiation of a nonnegative real number to a real power yields either the result of the exponentiation or infinity if the base is zero and the exponent is negative.
explanatories.measurable_const: This theorem states that the constant function mapping any element in a measurable space to a fixed value is measurable.
explanatories.Measurable.coe_nnreal_ennreal: If a function from a measurable space to the non-negative extended real numbers is measurable, then the function obtained by taking the image of that function in the non-negative real numbers is also measurable.
explanatories.MeasurableSet.inter: This theorem establishes that the intersection of two measurable sets is also a measurable set within the same measurable space.
explanatories.measurableSet_Iio: This theorem asserts that the set of all points less than a specific point in a linear ordered topological space is measurable.
explanatories.ENNReal.top_rpow_def: The theorem establishes that raising infinity to a positive power yields infinity, raising it to zero yields one, and raising it to a negative power yields zero.
explanatories.measurableSet_Ioi: This theorem asserts that the set of all points greater than a specific point in a linear ordered topological space is measurable.

ennreal.has_measurable_pow.fullDefinition: instance ENNReal.hasMeasurablePow : MeasurablePow ℝ≥0∞ ℝ := by   refine ⟨ENNReal.measurable_of_measurable_nnreal_prod ?_ ?_⟩   · simp_rw [ENNReal.coe_rpow_def]     refine Measurable.ite ?_ measurable_const (measurable_fst.pow measurable_snd).coe_nnreal_ennreal     exact       MeasurableSet.inter (measurable_fst (measurableSet_singleton 0))         (measurable_snd measurableSet_Iio)   · simp_rw [ENNReal.top_rpow_def]     refine Measurable.ite measurableSet_Ioi measurable_const ?_     exact Measurable.ite (measurableSet_singleton 0) measurable_const measurable_const

explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.coe_zero: This theorem states that the constant function equal to one, when viewed in the context of simple functions, is equivalent to the number one itself.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.coe_add: This theorem states that the product of two simple functions, when considered as measurable functions, is equivalent to the product of each simple function viewed as a measurable function.

explanatories.Function.Injective.addMonoid: This definition characterizes an additive monoid as a type equipped with a binary operation and an additive identity that can be injectively mapped to another additive monoid while preserving both the operation and the identity.
explanatories.ENNReal.coe_zero: This theorem states that the conversion of zero in the extended nonnegative real numbers to a standard nonnegative real number is equal to zero itself.
explanatories.NNReal.coe_zero: This theorem states that the coercion of zero as a nonnegative real number is equal to zero in the standard real number context.

MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.induction.code:
MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.induction.{u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_5} {γ : Type u_6} [MeasurableSpace α] [AddMonoid γ]
  {P : (α →ₛ γ) → Prop}
  (h_ind : ∀ (c : γ) {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s), P (piecewise s hs (const α c) (const α 0)))
  (h_add : ∀ ⦃f g : α →ₛ γ⦄, Disjoint (support ↑f) (support ↑g) → P f → P g → P (f + g)) (f : α →ₛ γ) : P f
MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.induction.comment:
To prove something for an arbitrary simple function, it suffices to show
that the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions and is closed under
addition (of functions with disjoint support).

It is possible to make the hypotheses in `h_add` a bit stronger, and such conditions can be added
once we need them (for example it is only necessary to consider the case where `g` is a multiple
of a characteristic function, and that this multiple doesn't appear in the image of `f`)

measure_theory.simple_func.induction.description: This theorem proves that a property holds for all simple functions by showing it is valid for characteristic functions defined on measurable sets and is preserved under addition for functions with disjoint supports.

Measurable.ennreal_induction.code:
Measurable.ennreal_induction.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α] {P : (α → ℝ≥0∞) → Prop}
  (h_ind : ∀ (c : ℝ≥0∞) ⦃s : Set α⦄, MeasurableSet s → P (s.indicator fun x => c))
  (h_add : ∀ ⦃f g : α → ℝ≥0∞⦄, Disjoint (support f) (support g) → Measurable f → Measurable g → P f → P g → P (f + g))
  (h_iSup :
    ∀ ⦃f : ℕ → α → ℝ≥0∞⦄, (∀ (n : ℕ), Measurable (f n)) → Monotone f → (∀ (n : ℕ), P (f n)) → P fun x => ⨆ n, f n x)
  ⦃f : α → ℝ≥0∞⦄ (hf : Measurable f) : P f
Measurable.ennreal_induction.comment:
To prove something for an arbitrary measurable function into `ℝ≥0∞`, it suffices to show
that the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions and is closed under addition
and supremum of increasing sequences of functions.

It is possible to make the hypotheses in the induction steps a bit stronger, and such conditions
can be added once we need them (for example in `h_add` it is only necessary to consider the sum of
a simple function with a multiple of a characteristic function and that the intersection
of their images is a subset of `{0}`.

  [SecondCountableTopology β] [MeasurableSpace β] [BorelSpace β] (s : Set β) (s_count : s.Countable) (s_dense : Dense s)
  (f : α → β)
  (h :
    ∀ p ∈ s,
      ∀ q ∈ s,
        p < q → ∃ u v, MeasurableSet u ∧ MeasurableSet v ∧ {x | f x < p} ⊆ u ∧ {x | q < f x} ⊆ v ∧ μ (u ∩ v) = 0) :
  AEMeasurable f μ
MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_of_exist_almo.comment:
If a function `f : α → β` is such that the level sets `{f < p}` and `{q < f}` have measurable
supersets which are disjoint up to measure zero when `p < q`, then `f` is almost-everywhere
measurable. It is even enough to have this for `p` and `q` in a countable dense set.

MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_of_exist_almost_disjoint_supersets.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace α}
  (μ : Measure α) {β : Type u_2} [CompleteLinearOrder β] [DenselyOrdered β] [TopologicalSpace β] [OrderTopology β]
  [SecondCountableTopology β] [MeasurableSpace β] [BorelSpace β] (s : Set β) (s_count : s.Countable) (s_dense : Dense s)
  (f : α → β)
  (h :
    ∀ p ∈ s,
      ∀ q ∈ s,
        p < q → ∃ u v, MeasurableSet u ∧ MeasurableSet v ∧ {x | f x < p} ⊆ u ∧ {x | q < f x} ⊆ v ∧ μ (u ∩ v) = 0) :
  AEMeasurable f μ
measure_theory.ae_measurable_of_exist_al.comment:
If a function `f : α → β` is such that the level sets `{f < p}` and `{q < f}` have measurable
supersets which are disjoint up to measure zero when `p < q`, then `f` is almost-everywhere
measurable. It is even enough to have this for `p` and `q` in a countable dense set.

MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.nearestPtInd.code:
MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.nearestPtInd.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α] [PseudoEMetricSpace α]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace α] (e : ℕ → α) : ℕ → α →ₛ ℕ
MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.nearestPtInd.comment:
`nearestPtInd e N x` is the index `k` such that `e k` is the nearest point to `x` among the
points `e 0`, ..., `e N`. If more than one point are at the same distance from `x`, then
`nearestPtInd e N x` returns the least of their indexes.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.const: This definition describes a simple function that assigns a constant value to every element of a given type within a measurable space.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.piecewise: This definition describes a way to construct a simple function that behaves like an if-then-else structure based on a measurable set and two other simple functions.
explanatories.Set.iInter: A function that computes the intersection of a collection of sets indexed by another set.
explanatories.EDist.edist: A distance function is defined on a type, returning non-negative extended real numbers between pairs of its elements.
explanatories.MeasurableSet.iInter: This theorem establishes that the intersection of a countable collection of measurable sets is also a measurable set within a given measurable space.
explanatories.measurableSet_lt: This theorem establishes that the set of points where one measurable function is less than another measurable function in a linear ordered, second countable topological space is measurable.
explanatories.measurable_edist_right: This theorem demonstrates that the function assigning to each point in a pseudo-emetric space the distance from that point to a fixed point is measurable within the associated measurable space.
explanatories.Set.piecewise: The piecewise function takes two functions and assigns one value on a specified set while assigning a different value outside that set.

MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.nearestPtInd.fullDefinition: noncomputable def nearestPtInd (e : ℕ → α) : ℕ → α →ₛ ℕ   | 0 => const α 0   | N + 1 =>     piecewise (⋂ k ≤ N, { x | edist (e (N + 1)) x < edist (e k) x })       (MeasurableSet.iInter fun _ =>         MeasurableSet.iInter fun _ =>           measurableSet_lt measurable_edist_right measurable_edist_right)       (const α <| N + 1) (nearestPtInd e N)
MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.nearestPtInd.description: The definition describes a function that returns the index of the nearest point to a given point among a list of specified points, favoring the smallest index in case of ties.

HasCompactSupport.exists_simpleFunc_approx_of_prod.{u_7, u_8, u_9} {X : Type u_7} {Y : Type u_8} {α : Type u_9} [Zero α]
  [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace X]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] [PseudoMetricSpace α] {f : X × Y → α} (hf : Continuous f) (h'f : HasCompactSupport f) {ε : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ g, ∀ (x : X × Y), dist (f x) (↑g x) < ε
HasCompactSupport.exists_simpleFunc_appr.comment:
A continuous function with compact support on a product space can be uniformly approximated by
simple functions. The subtlety is that we do not assume that the spaces are separable, so the
product of the Borel sigma algebras might not contain all open sets, but still it contains enough
of them to approximate compactly supported continuous functions.

HasCompactSupport.exists_simpleFunc_appr.description: The theorem demonstrates that any continuous function with compact support on a product space can be uniformly approximated by simple functions within a specified tolerance.

MeasureTheory.FinStronglyMeasurable.comment:
A function is `FinStronglyMeasurable` with respect to a measure if it is the limit of simple
functions with support with finite measure.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.

MeasureTheory.FinStronglyMeasurable.fullDefinition: def FinStronglyMeasurable [Zero β]     {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α → β) (μ : Measure α := by volume_tac) : Prop :=   ∃ fs : ℕ → α →ₛ β, (∀ n, μ (support (fs n)) < ∞) ∧ ∀ x, Tendsto (fun n => fs n x) atTop (𝓝 (f x))
MeasureTheory.FinStronglyMeasurable.description: A function is considered finitely strongly measurable with respect to a measure if it can be approximated as the limit of a sequence of simple functions that each have finite support.

MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.approxB.comment:
Similar to `stronglyMeasurable.approx`, but enforces that the norm of every function in the
sequence is less than `c` everywhere. If `‖f x‖ ≤ c` this sequence of simple functions verifies
`Tendsto (fun n => hf.approxBounded n x) atTop (𝓝 (f x))`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.map: This definition describes how to construct a new simple function by applying a given function to the output of an existing simple function.
explanatories.Min.min: This defines a minimum operation that takes two elements and returns the lesser of the two.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.min: This theorem states that if two functions converge to their respective limits in a topological space with an order-closed topology, then the function defined by taking the minimum of these two functions also converges to the minimum of those limits.
explanatories.List.map: This definition describes a function that transforms each element of a list by applying a specified function to it, producing a new list of the transformed elements.
explanatories.Multiset.map: This definition outlines a way to create a new multiset by applying a function to each element of an existing multiset, preserving the count of each element according to how many times the function produces the same output.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.map: This definition describes how to construct a new measure on one space from a measure on another space via a measurable function, resulting in a measure that is zero if the function is not almost everywhere measurable.

MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.approxB.fullDefinition: noncomputable def approxBounded {_ : MeasurableSpace α} [Norm β] [SMul ℝ β]     (hf : StronglyMeasurable f) (c : ℝ) : ℕ → SimpleFunc α β := fun n =>   (hf.approx n).map fun x => min 1 (c / ‖x‖) • x
MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.approxB.description: A function is approximated by a sequence of bounded simple functions that all have a norm less than a specified constant, ensuring convergence to the original function.

measure_theory.strongly_measurable.appro.comment:

sequence is less than `c` everywhere. If `‖f x‖ ≤ c` this sequence of simple functions verifies
`Tendsto (fun n => hf.approxBounded n x) atTop (𝓝 (f x))`.

MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.exists_.code:
MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.exists_spanning_measurableSet_norm_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2}
  {f : α → β} [SeminormedAddCommGroup β] {m m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (hm : m ≤ m0) (hf : StronglyMeasurable f)
  (μ : Measure α) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] :
  ∃ s, (∀ (n : ℕ), MeasurableSet (s n) ∧ μ (s n) < ⊤ ∧ ∀ x ∈ s n, ‖f x‖ ≤ ↑n) ∧ ⋃ i, s i = univ
MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.exists_.comment:
If a function `f` is strongly measurable w.r.t. a sub-σ-algebra `m` and the measure is σ-finite
on `m`, then there exists spanning measurable sets with finite measure on which `f` has bounded
norm. In particular, `f` is integrable on each of those sets.

MeasureTheory.Egorov.notConvergentSeq.code:
MeasureTheory.Egorov.notConvergentSeq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [MetricSpace β]
  [Preorder ι] (f : ι → α → β) (g : α → β) (n : ℕ) (j : ι) : Set α
MeasureTheory.Egorov.notConvergentSeq.comment:
Given a sequence of functions `f` and a function `g`, `notConvergentSeq f g n j` is the
set of elements such that `f k x` and `g x` are separated by at least `1 / (n + 1)` for some
`k ≥ j`.

This definition is useful for Egorov's theorem.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.dist: If two functions are strongly measurable, then the distance between their outputs is also strongly measurable.

MeasureTheory.Egorov.notConvergentSeq.fullDefinition: def notConvergentSeq [Preorder ι] (f : ι → α → β) (g : α → β) (n : ℕ) (j : ι) : Set α :=   ⋃ (k) (_ : j ≤ k), { x | 1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) < dist (f k x) (g x) }
MeasureTheory.Egorov.notConvergentSeq.description: For a sequence of functions and a reference function, the definition identifies the set of points where the values of the sequence, after a particular index, deviate from the reference function by at least a specified margin.

MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_t.comment:
**Egorov's theorem**: If `f : ι → α → β` is a sequence of strongly measurable functions that
converges to `g : α → β` almost everywhere on a measurable set `s` of finite measure,
then for all `ε > 0`, there exists a subset `t ⊆ s` such that `μ t ≤ ε` and `f` converges to `g`
uniformly on `s \ t`. We require the index type `ι` to be countable, and usually `ι = ℕ`.

In other words, a sequence of almost everywhere convergent functions converges uniformly except on
an arbitrarily small set.

MeasureTheory.Measure.aeEqSetoid.comment:
The equivalence relation of being almost everywhere equal for almost everywhere strongly
measurable functions.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable: A function is considered almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a measure if it is equal to the limit of a sequence of simple functions except on a set of measure zero.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.ae_eq_refl: This theorem asserts that a function is almost everywhere equal to itself with respect to a measure.
explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element from the base type that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.ae_eq_symm: This theorem states that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a measure, then they are also equal almost everywhere in the reverse order.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.ae_eq_trans: This theorem states that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a measure, and the second function is also equal almost everywhere to a third function, then the first and third functions are equal almost everywhere as well.

MeasureTheory.Measure.aeEqSetoid.fullDefinition: def Measure.aeEqSetoid (μ : Measure α) : Setoid { f : α → β // AEStronglyMeasurable f μ } :=   ⟨fun f g => (f : α → β) =ᵐ[μ] g, fun {f} => ae_eq_refl f.val, fun {_ _} => ae_eq_symm,     fun {_ _ _} => ae_eq_trans⟩
MeasureTheory.Measure.aeEqSetoid.description: The defined setoid characterizes the equivalence relation of almost everywhere equality among almost everywhere strongly measurable functions with respect to a specified measure.

strongly measurable functions are equivalent if they agree almost everywhere, i.e.,
they differ on a set of measure `0`.

Composition of an almost everywhere equal function and a quasi measure preserving function.

See also `AEEqFun.compMeasurePreserving`.
