MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.compMeasurePreserv.fullDefinition: def compMeasurePreserving (g : β →ₘ[ν] γ) (f : α → β) (hf : MeasurePreserving f μ ν) : α →ₘ[μ] γ :=   g.compQuasiMeasurePreserving f hf.quasiMeasurePreserving
MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.compMeasurePreserv.description: The definition describes a way to obtain an almost everywhere measurable function on one space by composing it with a measure-preserving function that maps to another space.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.ae: The "almost everywhere" filter represents the collection of sets that differ from a given set by at most a collection of co-null sets.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.compQuasiMeasurePr: The definition describes a method for composing an almost everywhere equal function with a quasi measure preserving function to produce a new function that is also almost everywhere equal with respect to a given measure.

MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.coeFn_compQuasiMea.description: The theorem establishes that a function which is quasi-measure preserving when composed with an almost everywhere measurable function remains almost everywhere equal to the composition of the two functions.

  {μ : Measure α} [TopologicalSpace β] [TopologicalSpace γ] (g : β → γ) (hg : Continuous g) (f : α →ₘ[μ] β) : α →ₘ[μ] γ
MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.comp.comment:
Given a continuous function `g : β → γ`, and an almost everywhere equal function `[f] : α →ₘ β`,
return the equivalence class of `g ∘ f`, i.e., the almost everywhere equal function
`[g ∘ f] : α →ₘ γ`.

return the equivalence class of `g ∘ f`, i.e., the almost everywhere equal function

Given a continuous function `g : β → γ → δ`, and almost everywhere equal functions
`[f₁] : α →ₘ β` and `[f₂] : α →ₘ γ`, return the equivalence class of the function
`fun a => g (f₁ a) (f₂ a)`, i.e., the almost everywhere equal function
`[fun a => g (f₁ a) (f₂ a)] : α →ₘ γ`

MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.comp₂Measurable.code:
MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.comp₂Measurable.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {γ : Type u_3} {δ : Type u_4}
  [MeasurableSpace α] {μ : Measure α} [TopologicalSpace β] [TopologicalSpace γ] [TopologicalSpace δ] [MeasurableSpace β]
  [PseudoMetrizableSpace β] [BorelSpace β] [MeasurableSpace γ] [PseudoMetrizableSpace γ] [BorelSpace γ]
  [SecondCountableTopologyEither β γ] [MeasurableSpace δ] [PseudoMetrizableSpace δ] [OpensMeasurableSpace δ]
  [SecondCountableTopology δ] (g : β → γ → δ) (hg : Measurable (uncurry g)) (f₁ : α →ₘ[μ] β) (f₂ : α →ₘ[μ] γ) :
  α →ₘ[μ] δ
MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.comp₂Measurable.comment:
Given a measurable function `g : β → γ → δ`, and almost everywhere equal functions
`[f₁] : α →ₘ β` and `[f₂] : α →ₘ γ`, return the equivalence class of the function
`fun a => g (f₁ a) (f₂ a)`, i.e., the almost everywhere equal function
`[fun a => g (f₁ a) (f₂ a)] : α →ₘ γ`. This requires `δ` to have second-countable topology.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.compMeasurable: The definition establishes a method for obtaining the equivalence class of the composition of a measurable function with an almost everywhere equal function, ensuring the result remains almost everywhere equal to the original outputs in the codomain with specific topological conditions.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.pair: The pair of two measurable functions is itself a measurable function that maps each input to the corresponding outputs of the two functions as a tuple.

MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.comp₂Measurable.fullDefinition: def comp₂Measurable (g : β → γ → δ) (hg : Measurable (uncurry g)) (f₁ : α →ₘ[μ] β)     (f₂ : α →ₘ[μ] γ) : α →ₘ[μ] δ :=   compMeasurable _ hg (f₁.pair f₂)
MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.comp₂Measurable.description: The definition describes a method for constructing an almost everywhere equivalent function that results from applying a measurable function to two almost everywhere equal functions, subject to specific topological conditions.

MeasureTheory.exists_Lp_half.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} (E : Type u_2) {m : MeasurableSpace α} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  (μ : Measure α) (p : ℝ≥0∞) {δ : ℝ≥0∞} (hδ : δ ≠ 0) :
  ∃ η,
    0 < η ∧
      ∀ (f g : α → E),
        AEStronglyMeasurable f μ → AEStronglyMeasurable g μ → snorm f p μ ≤ η → snorm g p μ ≤ η → snorm (f + g) p μ < δ
MeasureTheory.exists_Lp_half.comment:
Technical lemma to control the addition of functions in `L^p` even for `p < 1`: Given `δ > 0`,
there exists `η` such that two functions bounded by `η` in `L^p` have a sum bounded by `δ`. One
could take `η = δ / 2` for `p ≥ 1`, but the point of the lemma is that it works also for `p < 1`.

MeasureTheory.exists_Lp_half.description: This theorem asserts that for any positive threshold, there exists a bound such that if two almost everywhere strongly measurable functions are each below this bound in an L-p seminorm, their sum will be bounded by a given positive value, even when the exponent is less than one.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm: This definition describes a seminorm for measurable functions that corresponds to different expressions depending on the value of p, including integrating the p-th power of the norm, taking the essential supremum, and being zero for p equal to zero.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm_congr_ae: This theorem states that if two measurable functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a measure, then their seminorms are also equal.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.coeFn_add: The theorem states that the product of two almost everywhere measurable functions is itself almost everywhere measurable and is equal to the product of their respective equivalence classes almost everywhere under the given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm_add_lt_top: This theorem establishes that if two functions are each in the \( L^p \) space with respect to a measure, then their sum will have a finite \( L^p \) seminorm.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.aestronglyMeasurab: Any function that is almost everywhere equal with respect to a measure is also considered almost everywhere strongly measurable under that measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.coeFn_zero: The constant function equal to one is almost everywhere equal to the value one with respect to the given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm_zero: This theorem states that the seminorm of a measurable function evaluated at zero for any non-negative exponent is equal to zero.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.coeFn_neg: The theorem states that the almost everywhere inverse of an almost everywhere measurable function is equal to the almost everywhere measurable function's inverse, when considered with respect to the given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm_neg: This theorem states that the seminorm of the negative of a measurable function with respect to a given measure is equal to the seminorm of the function itself.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.aestron: If a function is strongly measurable, then it is also almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Memℒp.aestronglyMeasurable: This theorem states that if a function belongs to the space of p-integrable functions with respect to a measure, then it is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to that measure.
explanatories.AEMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable: In a space with a second countable topology, a function that is almost everywhere measurable is also strongly measurable.

MeasureTheory.Lp.fullDefinition: def Lp {α} (E : Type*) {m : MeasurableSpace α} [NormedAddCommGroup E] (p : ℝ≥0∞)     (μ : Measure α := by volume_tac) : AddSubgroup (α →ₘ[μ] E) where   carrier := { f | snorm f p μ < ∞ }   zero_mem' := by simp [snorm_congr_ae AEEqFun.coeFn_zero, snorm_zero]   add_mem' {f g} hf hg := by     simp [snorm_congr_ae (AEEqFun.coeFn_add f g),       snorm_add_lt_top ⟨f.aestronglyMeasurable, hf⟩ ⟨g.aestronglyMeasurable, hg⟩]   neg_mem' {f} hf := by rwa [Set.mem_setOf_eq, snorm_congr_ae (AEEqFun.coeFn_neg f), snorm_neg]
MeasureTheory.Lp.description: The Lp space is defined as an additively closed subgroup of measurable functions from a measurable space to a normed group, equipped with a specified p-norm and measure.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm_congr_ae: This theorem states that if two measurable functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a measure, then their seminorms are also equal.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.aestronglyMeasurab: Any function that is almost everywhere equal with respect to a measure is also considered almost everywhere strongly measurable under that measure.

explanatories.Eq.trans_le: A theorem that establishes that in a partially ordered structure, if one element is equal to a second and that second element is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

explanatories.AEMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable: In a space with a second countable topology, a function that is almost everywhere measurable is also strongly measurable.

MeasureTheory.Lp.instNormedAddCommGroup.fullDefinition: instance instNormedAddCommGroup [hp : Fact (1 ≤ p)] : NormedAddCommGroup (Lp E p μ) :=   { AddGroupNorm.toNormedAddCommGroup       { toFun := (norm : Lp E p μ → ℝ)         map_zero' := norm_zero         neg' := by simp         add_le' := fun f g => by           suffices (‖f + g‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ‖f‖₊ + ‖g‖₊ from mod_cast this           simp only [Lp.nnnorm_coe_ennreal]           exact (snorm_congr_ae (AEEqFun.coeFn_add _ _)).trans_le             (snorm_add_le (Lp.aestronglyMeasurable _) (Lp.aestronglyMeasurable _) hp.out)         eq_zero_of_map_eq_zero' := fun f =>           (norm_eq_zero_iff <| zero_lt_one.trans_le hp.1).1 } with     edist := edist     edist_dist := Lp.edist_dist }
MeasureTheory.Lp.instNormedAddCommGroup.description: The Lp space of measurable functions under a given measure is equipped with a normed additive commutative group structure when the parameter p is at least one.

  {μ : Measure α} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {f : ℕ → α → E} (hf : ∀ (n : ℕ), AEStronglyMeasurable (f n) μ) (f_lim : α → E)
  {B : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞} (hB : ∑' (i : ℕ), B i ≠ ⊤) (h_cau : ∀ (N n m : ℕ), N ≤ n → N ≤ m → snorm (f n - f m) p μ < B N)
  (h_lim : ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => f n x) atTop (𝓝 (f_lim x))) :

explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable: A function is considered almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a measure if it is equal to the limit of a sequence of simple functions except on a set of measure zero.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm: This definition describes a seminorm for measurable functions that corresponds to different expressions depending on the value of p, including integrating the p-th power of the norm, taking the essential supremum, and being zero for p equal to zero.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.

measure_theory.Lp.cauchy_tendsto_of_tend.description: If a sequence of measurable functions converges almost everywhere to a limit and satisfies a certain Cauchy criterion in the Lp space, then the norm of their difference from the limit converges to zero.

An additive subgroup of `Lp E p μ`, consisting of the equivalence classes which contain a

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.comp: The composition of an almost everywhere equal function with a continuous function produces another function that is also almost everywhere equal under the same measure.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.comp: A theorem stating that the composition of two functions that tend to maps between respective filters also results in a function that tends to map from the original filter to the final one.
explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.
explanatories.AddSubgroup.addSubgroupOf: This definition describes the intersection of two additive subgroups as a subgroup that can be viewed as a subset of one of those subgroups.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.toAEEqFunAddHom: This definition describes a multiplicative homomorphism that maps continuous functions from one measurable space to equivalence classes of almost everywhere measurable functions with respect to a given measure.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.comp: This definition states that the composition of morphisms between additive monoids results in a morphism that also operates within the framework of additive monoids.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.range: This definition describes the range of an additive monoid homomorphism from one additive group to another as an additive subgroup of the target group.
explanatories.NormedAddGroupHom.range: This definition describes the range of a bounded homomorphism between seminormed additive groups as a subgroup of the codomain that inherits a seminormed additive group structure.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.LinearMap.range: This definition states that the range of a linear map between modules is a submodule of the codomain module.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp: The composition of bounded linear maps results in another bounded linear map.
explanatories.Function.Injective.comp: This theorem does not contain any information or statement to interpret.

MeasureTheory.Lp.boundedContinuousFuncti.fullDefinition: def MeasureTheory.Lp.boundedContinuousFunction : AddSubgroup (Lp E p μ) :=   AddSubgroup.addSubgroupOf     ((ContinuousMap.toAEEqFunAddHom μ).comp (toContinuousMapAddHom α E)).range (Lp E p μ)
MeasureTheory.Lp.boundedContinuousFuncti.description: The set of equivalence classes in the Lp space that have a bounded continuous representative forms an additive subgroup.

ContinuousMap.toLp.comment:
The bounded linear map of considering a continuous function on a compact finite-measure
space `α` as an element of `Lp`.  By definition, the norm on `C(α, E)` is the sup-norm, transferred
from the space `α →ᵇ E` of bounded continuous functions, so this construction is just a matter of
transferring the structure from `BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp` along the isometry.

ContinuousMap.toLp.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (p : ℝ≥0∞) (μ : Measure α)
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [TopologicalSpace α] [BorelSpace α] [SecondCountableTopologyEither α E] [CompactSpace α]
  [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (𝕜 : Type u_5) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] : C(α, E) →L[𝕜] ↥(Lp E p μ)
continuous_map.to_Lp.comment:
The bounded linear map of considering a continuous function on a compact finite-measure
space `α` as an element of `Lp`.  By definition, the norm on `C(α, E)` is the sup-norm, transferred
from the space `α →ᵇ E` of bounded continuous functions, so this construction is just a matter of
transferring the structure from `BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp` along the isometry.

MeasureTheory.Lp.instCovariantClassLE.description: This definition specifies that the space of equivalence classes of measurable functions forms a covariant class with respect to addition and the order of inequality.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.coeFn_inf: The theorem states that the almost everywhere equality of the infimum of two almost everywhere measurable functions is equivalent to the pointwise infimum of their values almost everywhere with respect to a measure.

MeasureTheory.Lp.instLattice.fullDefinition: instance instLattice : Lattice (Lp E p μ) :=   Subtype.lattice     (fun f g hf hg => by       rw [mem_Lp_iff_memℒp] at *       exact (memℒp_congr_ae (AEEqFun.coeFn_sup _ _)).mpr (hf.sup hg))     fun f g hf hg => by     rw [mem_Lp_iff_memℒp] at *     exact (memℒp_congr_ae (AEEqFun.coeFn_inf _ _)).mpr (hf.inf hg)
MeasureTheory.Lp.instLattice.description: This definition establishes that the space of equivalence classes of measurable functions with respect to a measure forms a lattice structure under pointwise operations.

explanatories.ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal: This theorem establishes that the comparison of two positive extended nonnegative real numbers in the standard real number system is equivalent to their comparison in the extended nonnegative real number system, under the condition that neither number is infinity.

explanatories.HasSolidNorm.solid: This theorem states that if the absolute value of one element is less than or equal to that of another in a lattice with a solid norm, then the norm of the first element is also less than or equal to the norm of the second element.

MeasureTheory.Lp.instNormedLatticeAddCom.fullDefinition: noncomputable instance instNormedLatticeAddCommGroup [Fact (1 ≤ p)] :     NormedLatticeAddCommGroup (Lp E p μ) :=   { Lp.instLattice, Lp.instNormedAddCommGroup with     add_le_add_left := fun f g => add_le_add_left     solid := fun f g hfg => by       rw [← coeFn_le] at hfg       simp_rw [Lp.norm_def, ENNReal.toReal_le_toReal (Lp.snorm_ne_top f) (Lp.snorm_ne_top g)]       refine snorm_mono_ae ?_       filter_upwards [hfg, Lp.coeFn_abs f, Lp.coeFn_abs g] with x hx hxf hxg       rw [hxf, hxg] at hx       exact HasSolidNorm.solid hx }
MeasureTheory.Lp.instNormedLatticeAddCom.description: This definition states that the space of equivalence classes of measurable functions equipped with a suitable norm structure forms a normed lattice additive commutative group.

MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure.comment:
A sequence of functions `f` is said to converge in measure to some function `g` if for all
`ε > 0`, the measure of the set `{x | ε ≤ dist (f i x) (g x)}` tends to 0 as `i` converges along
some given filter `l`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.

MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure.fullDefinition: def TendstoInMeasure [Dist E] {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : ι → α → E) (l : Filter ι)     (g : α → E) : Prop :=   ∀ ε, 0 < ε → Tendsto (fun i => μ { x | ε ≤ dist (f i x) (g x) }) l (𝓝 0)
MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure.description: This definition describes a concept of convergence in measure for a sequence of functions, indicating that a sequence converges to a limit function if the measure of the set where their distances exceed a specified threshold approaches zero as the sequence progresses.

where `‖f x‖ ≥ ε` is finite for all positive `ε`.

MeasureTheory.withDensitySMulLI.fullDefinition: noncomputable def withDensitySMulLI {f : α → ℝ≥0} (f_meas : Measurable f) :     Lp E 1 (μ.withDensity fun x => f x) →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp E 1 μ where   toFun u := (memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas u).toLp _   map_add' := by     intro u v     ext1     filter_upwards [(memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas u).coeFn_toLp,       (memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas v).coeFn_toLp,       (memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas (u + v)).coeFn_toLp,       Lp.coeFn_add ((memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas u).toLp _)         ((memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas v).toLp _),       (ae_withDensity_iff f_meas.coe_nnreal_ennreal).1 (Lp.coeFn_add u v)]     intro x hu hv huv h' h''     rw [huv, h', Pi.add_apply, hu, hv]     rcases eq_or_ne (f x) 0 with (hx | hx)     · simp only [hx, zero_smul, add_zero]     · rw [h'' _, Pi.add_apply, smul_add]       simpa only [Ne, ENNReal.coe_eq_zero] using hx   map_smul' := by     intro r u     ext1     filter_upwards [(ae_withDensity_iff f_meas.coe_nnreal_ennreal).1 (Lp.coeFn_smul r u),       (memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas (r • u)).coeFn_toLp,       Lp.coeFn_smul r ((memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas u).toLp _),       (memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas u).coeFn_toLp]     intro x h h' h'' h'''     rw [RingHom.id_apply, h', h'', Pi.smul_apply, h''']     rcases eq_or_ne (f x) 0 with (hx | hx)     · simp only [hx, zero_smul, smul_zero]     · rw [h _, smul_comm, Pi.smul_apply]       simpa only [Ne, ENNReal.coe_eq_zero] using hx   norm_map' := by     intro u     -- Porting note: Lean can't infer types of `AddHom.coe_mk`.     simp only [snorm, LinearMap.coe_mk,       AddHom.coe_mk (M := Lp E 1 (μ.withDensity fun x => f x)) (N := Lp E 1 μ), Lp.norm_toLp,       one_ne_zero, ENNReal.one_ne_top, ENNReal.one_toReal, if_false, snorm', ENNReal.rpow_one,       _root_.div_one, Lp.norm_def]     rw [lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul_non_measurable _ f_meas.coe_nnreal_ennreal         (Filter.eventually_of_forall fun x => ENNReal.coe_lt_top)]     congr 1     apply lintegral_congr_ae     filter_upwards [(memℒ1_smul_of_L1_withDensity f_meas u).coeFn_toLp] with x hx     rw [hx, Pi.mul_apply]     change (‖(f x : ℝ) • u x‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) = (f x : ℝ≥0∞) * (‖u x‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞)     simp only [nnnorm_smul, NNReal.nnnorm_eq, ENNReal.coe_mul]

MeasureTheory.UnifIntegrable.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup β] :
  {x : MeasurableSpace α} → (ι → α → β) → ℝ≥0∞ → Measure α → Prop
MeasureTheory.UnifIntegrable.comment:
Uniform integrability in the measure theory sense.

A sequence of functions `f` is said to be uniformly integrable if for all `ε > 0`, there exists
some `δ > 0` such that for all sets `s` with measure less than `δ`, the Lp-norm of `f i`
restricted on `s` is less than `ε`.

Uniform integrability is also known as uniformly absolutely continuous integrals.

MeasureTheory.UnifIntegrable.description: The definition characterizes a sequence of functions as uniformly integrable if, for every small positive threshold, there exists a corresponding small measure threshold ensuring the restricted integrals over sets of small measure are also small.

  (hp' : p ≠ ⊤) (hf : ∀ (n : ℕ), Memℒp (f n) p μ) (hg : Memℒp g p μ) :
  TendstoInMeasure μ f atTop g ∧ UnifIntegrable f p μ ↔ Tendsto (fun n => snorm (f n - g) p μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

only if it is uniformly integrable and converges to `g` in measure.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.aestronglyMeasu: Every simple function is associated with a measure that exhibits almost everywhere strong measurability.
explanatories.AEMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable: In a space with a second countable topology, a function that is almost everywhere measurable is also strongly measurable.
explanatories.BorelSpace.mk: A type equipped with a topological structure and a measurable space is definitively a Borel space if the measurable structure coincides with the Borel σ-algebra generated by its open sets.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.mk: This definition describes a construction of a function that is almost everywhere strongly measurable, ensuring it is equivalent to the original function in terms of measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.mk: The construction creates the equivalence class of an almost everywhere measurable function, identifying it with other functions that are almost everywhere equal under a specified measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.mk_add_mk: The product of two almost everywhere strongly measurable functions is also almost everywhere strongly measurable and can be represented by the product of their respective measurable constructions.
explanatories.AddSubgroup.coe_add: This theorem establishes that the image of the sum of two elements from an additive subgroup corresponds to the sum of their respective images in the additive group.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.mk_eq_mk: The equality of two almost everywhere strongly measurable functions corresponds to the condition that they are equal almost everywhere with respect to the specified measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.coe_add: This theorem states that the product of two simple functions, when considered as measurable functions, is equivalent to the product of each simple function viewed as a measurable function.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.neg_mk: The theorem demonstrates that the inverse of an almost everywhere strongly measurable function can be expressed in terms of the inverse of the function itself, preserving the property of almost everywhere equality.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.coe_neg: This theorem establishes that the inversion of a simple function, when represented as a coefficient, is equal to the coefficient of its inverse.
explanatories.AddSubgroup.coe_neg: This theorem states that the negation of an element in an additive subgroup can be expressed as the image of the negation of its representative in the subgroup.
explanatories.SMul.mk: This theorem introduces a way to create a scalar multiplication structure for a type by specifying a function that describes how elements of one type act on elements of another type through multiplication.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.NormedSpace.mk: This theorem constructs a normed space from a seminormed additive group and a normed field, given a condition on the interaction between the scalar multiplication and the norms.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.aestron: If a function is strongly measurable, then it is also almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a given measure.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.CovariantClass.mk: This theorem shows that if a covariant property is satisfied by a specific action on one type with respect to a relation, then this property can be organized into a coherent structure classified as a covariant class.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Memℒp.aestronglyMeasurable: This theorem states that if a function belongs to the space of p-integrable functions with respect to a measure, then it is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to that measure.

MeasureTheory.Lp.simpleFunc.fullDefinition: def simpleFunc : AddSubgroup (Lp E p μ) where   carrier := { f : Lp E p μ | ∃ s : α →ₛ E, (AEEqFun.mk s s.aestronglyMeasurable : α →ₘ[μ] E) = f }   zero_mem' := ⟨0, rfl⟩   add_mem' := by     rintro f g ⟨s, hs⟩ ⟨t, ht⟩     use s + t     simp only [← hs, ← ht, AEEqFun.mk_add_mk, AddSubgroup.coe_add, AEEqFun.mk_eq_mk,       SimpleFunc.coe_add]   neg_mem' := by     rintro f ⟨s, hs⟩     use -s     simp only [← hs, AEEqFun.neg_mk, SimpleFunc.coe_neg, AEEqFun.mk_eq_mk, AddSubgroup.coe_neg]
MeasureTheory.Lp.simpleFunc.description: The definition describes a subspace of Lp consisting of equivalence classes formed by integrable simple functions.

MeasureTheory.Lp.simpleFunc.induction.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_4} [MeasurableSpace α]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] {p : ℝ≥0∞} {μ : Measure α} (hp_pos : p ≠ 0) (hp_ne_top : p ≠ ⊤)
  {P : ↥(simpleFunc E p μ) → Prop}
  (h_ind : ∀ (c : E) {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hμs : μ s < ⊤), P (indicatorConst p hs ⋯ c))
  (h_add :
    ∀ ⦃f g : α →ₛ E⦄ (hf : Memℒp (↑f) p μ) (hg : Memℒp (↑g) p μ),
      Disjoint (support ↑f) (support ↑g) → P (toLp f hf) → P (toLp g hg) → P (toLp f hf + toLp g hg))
  (f : ↥(simpleFunc E p μ)) : P f
MeasureTheory.Lp.simpleFunc.induction.comment:
To prove something for an arbitrary `Lp` simple function, with `0 < p < ∞`, it suffices to show
that the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions of finite-measure measurable
sets and is closed under addition (of functions with disjoint support).

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Lp.simpleFunc.toLp: This definition constructs the equivalence class of a simple function that belongs to the Lp space, provided it satisfies specific integrability conditions.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Lp.simpleFunc.indicatorCon: The definition describes a constant indicator function associated with a measurable set that has finite measure, represented as a simple function in the Lp space.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc.induction: This theorem proves that a property holds for all simple functions by showing it is valid for characteristic functions defined on measurable sets and is preserved under addition for functions with disjoint supports.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Lp.simpleFunc.induction: The theorem demonstrates that to prove a property for all Lp simple functions with a finite exponent, it is sufficient to verify that the property holds for constant functions on measurable sets of finite measure and is preserved under addition for functions with disjoint supports.

MeasureTheory.Lp.induction.description: The theorem establishes that a property defined for simple functions in the Lp space can be generalized to all functions in Lp by demonstrating its validity for characteristic functions, ensuring closure under addition, and confirming that the set of functions satisfying the property is closed.

MeasureTheory.Memℒp.induction.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_4} [MeasurableSpace α] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  {p : ℝ≥0∞} {μ : Measure α} [_i : Fact (1 ≤ p)] (hp_ne_top : p ≠ ⊤) (P : (α → E) → Prop)
  (h_ind : ∀ (c : E) ⦃s : Set α⦄, MeasurableSet s → μ s < ⊤ → P (s.indicator fun x => c))
  (h_add : ∀ ⦃f g : α → E⦄, Disjoint (support f) (support g) → Memℒp f p μ → Memℒp g p μ → P f → P g → P (f + g))
  (h_closed : IsClosed {f | P ↑↑f}) (h_ae : ∀ ⦃f g : α → E⦄, f =ᶠ[ae μ] g → Memℒp f p μ → P f → P g) ⦃f : α → E⦄ :
  Memℒp f p μ → P f
MeasureTheory.Memℒp.induction.comment:
To prove something for an arbitrary `Memℒp` function in a second countable
Borel normed group, it suffices to show that
* the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions;
* is closed under addition;
* the set of functions in the `Lᵖ` space for which the property holds is closed.
* the property is closed under the almost-everywhere equal relation.

It is possible to make the hypotheses in the induction steps a bit stronger, and such conditions
can be added once we need them (for example in `h_add` it is only necessary to consider the sum of
a simple function with a multiple of a characteristic function and that the intersection
of their images is a subset of `{0}`).

MeasureTheory.Integrable.induction.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_4} [MeasurableSpace α] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  {μ : Measure α} (P : (α → E) → Prop)
  (h_ind : ∀ (c : E) ⦃s : Set α⦄, MeasurableSet s → μ s < ⊤ → P (s.indicator fun x => c))
  (h_add : ∀ ⦃f g : α → E⦄, Disjoint (support f) (support g) → Integrable f μ → Integrable g μ → P f → P g → P (f + g))
  (h_closed : IsClosed {f | P ↑↑f}) (h_ae : ∀ ⦃f g : α → E⦄, f =ᶠ[ae μ] g → Integrable f μ → P f → P g) ⦃f : α → E⦄ :
  Integrable f μ → P f
MeasureTheory.Integrable.induction.comment:
To prove something for an arbitrary integrable function in a normed group,
it suffices to show that
* the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions;
* is closed under addition;
* the set of functions in the `L¹` space for which the property holds is closed.
* the property is closed under the almost-everywhere equal relation.

It is possible to make the hypotheses in the induction steps a bit stronger, and such conditions
can be added once we need them (for example in `h_add` it is only necessary to consider the sum of
a simple function with a multiple of a characteristic function and that the intersection
of their images is a subset of `{0}`).

MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.code:
MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.{u_1, u_3} {X : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace X] [TopologicalSpace X]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] (f : X → E) (s : Set X) (μ : Measure X := by volume_tac) : Prop
MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.comment:
A function `f : X → E` is *locally integrable on s*, for `s ⊆ X`, if for every `x ∈ s` there is
a neighbourhood of `x` within `s` on which `f` is integrable. (Note this is, in general, strictly
weaker than local integrability with respect to `μ.restrict s`.)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.fullDefinition: def LocallyIntegrableOn (f : X → E) (s : Set X) (μ : Measure X := by volume_tac) : Prop :=   ∀ x : X, x ∈ s → IntegrableAtFilter f (𝓝[s] x) μ
MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrableOn.description: A function is considered locally integrable on a specified set if for every point in that set, there exists a neighborhood around that point where the function can be integrated.

MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable'.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace β]
  (m : MeasurableSpace α) : {x : MeasurableSpace α} → (α → β) → Measure α → Prop
MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable'.comment:
A function `f` verifies `AEStronglyMeasurable' m f μ` if it is `μ`-a.e. equal to
an `m`-strongly measurable function. This is similar to `AEStronglyMeasurable`, but the
`MeasurableSpace` structures used for the measurability statement and for the measure are
different.
MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable'.fullDefinition: def AEStronglyMeasurable' {α β} [TopologicalSpace β] (m : MeasurableSpace α)     {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α → β) (μ : Measure α) : Prop :=   ∃ g : α → β, StronglyMeasurable[m] g ∧ f =ᵐ[μ] g
MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable'.description: This definition describes a condition for a function to be almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function with respect to different measurable space structures and a specified measure.

measure_theory.ae_strongly_measurable'.fullDefinition: def AEStronglyMeasurable' {α β} [TopologicalSpace β] (m : MeasurableSpace α)     {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α → β) (μ : Measure α) : Prop :=   ∃ g : α → β, StronglyMeasurable[m] g ∧ f =ᵐ[μ] g

If the restriction to a set `s` of a σ-algebra `m` is included in the restriction to `s` of
another σ-algebra `m₂` (hypothesis `hs`), the set `s` is `m` measurable and a function `f` almost

`m₂`-ae-strongly-measurable.

MeasureTheory.lpMeasSubgroup.fullDefinition: def lpMeasSubgroup (m : MeasurableSpace α) [MeasurableSpace α] (p : ℝ≥0∞) (μ : Measure α) :     AddSubgroup (Lp F p μ) where   carrier := {f : Lp F p μ | AEStronglyMeasurable' m f μ}   zero_mem' := ⟨(0 : α → F), @stronglyMeasurable_zero _ _ m _ _, Lp.coeFn_zero _ _ _⟩   add_mem' {f g} hf hg := (hf.add hg).congr (Lp.coeFn_add f g).symm   neg_mem' {f} hf := AEStronglyMeasurable'.congr hf.neg (Lp.coeFn_neg f).symm
MeasureTheory.lpMeasSubgroup.description: This definition identifies a subspace of functions in the space of measurable functions which are almost everywhere equal to another function that is strongly measurable with respect to a specified measure.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable': This definition describes a condition for a function to be almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function with respect to different measurable space structures and a specified measure.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.symm: A theorem asserting that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then they are also equal almost everywhere in the reverse order with respect to that filter.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable'.cong: This theorem establishes that if one function is almost everywhere equal to another function and the first function is almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function, then the second function is also almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function under the same conditions.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.add: The product of two strongly measurable functions is also strongly measurable.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.add: A theorem stating that if two pairs of functions are eventually equal under a given filter, then their sum is also eventually equal under the same filter.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable'.add: This theorem asserts that if two functions are both almost everywhere equal to strongly measurable functions, then their sum is also almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function under the same measure conditions.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.neg: The inverse of a strongly measurable function is also strongly measurable, provided the inverse operation is continuous.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable'.neg: This theorem states that if a function is almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function, then its negation is also almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function under the same measure conditions.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Lp: The Lp space is defined as an additively closed subgroup of measurable functions from a measurable space to a normed group, equipped with a specified p-norm and measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_add: The sum of two functions in the Lp space equals the almost everywhere limit of the sum of their measurable representatives under the given measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.stronglyMeasurable_zero: The theorem establishes that the constant function equal to one is strongly measurable in any measurable space.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_zero: The zero function is almost everywhere equal to the representative function assigned to the zero element in the Lp space under the specified measure.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Lp.coeFn_neg: The negative of a function in the Lp space is almost everywhere equal to the negative of the original function when considered under the specified measure.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.neg: A theorem stating that if two functions are eventually equal under a filter, then their negations are also eventually equal under the same filter.
explanatories.IsometryEquiv.symm: The inverse of an isometric isomorphism is also an isometric isomorphism.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a linear isometry equivalence, enabling a bijection between two seminormed vector spaces that preserves their respective structures when reversed.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Memℒp.add: This theorem states that if two functions are in the Lp space with respect to a measure, then their sum is also in the same Lp space.

measure_theory.Lp_meas_subgroup.fullDefinition: def lpMeasSubgroup (m : MeasurableSpace α) [MeasurableSpace α] (p : ℝ≥0∞) (μ : Measure α) :     AddSubgroup (Lp F p μ) where   carrier := {f : Lp F p μ | AEStronglyMeasurable' m f μ}   zero_mem' := ⟨(0 : α → F), @stronglyMeasurable_zero _ _ m _ _, Lp.coeFn_zero _ _ _⟩   add_mem' {f g} hf hg := (hf.add hg).congr (Lp.coeFn_add f g).symm   neg_mem' {f} hf := AEStronglyMeasurable'.congr hf.neg (Lp.coeFn_neg f).symm
measure_theory.Lp_meas_subgroup.description: This definition identifies a subspace of functions in the space of measurable functions which are almost everywhere equal to another function that is strongly measurable with respect to a specified measure.

MeasureTheory.Memℒp.induction_stronglyMe.code:
MeasureTheory.Memℒp.induction_stronglyMeasurable.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {F : Type u_3} {p : ℝ≥0∞}
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] {m m0 : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (hm : m ≤ m0)
  (hp_ne_top : p ≠ ⊤) (P : (α → F) → Prop)
  (h_ind : ∀ (c : F) ⦃s : Set α⦄, MeasurableSet s → μ s < ⊤ → P (s.indicator fun x => c))
  (h_add :
    ∀ ⦃f g : α → F⦄,
      Disjoint (Function.support f) (Function.support g) →
        Memℒp f p μ → Memℒp g p μ → StronglyMeasurable f → StronglyMeasurable g → P f → P g → P (f + g))
  (h_closed : IsClosed {f | P ↑↑↑f}) (h_ae : ∀ ⦃f g : α → F⦄, f =ᶠ[ae μ] g → Memℒp f p μ → P f → P g) ⦃f : α → F⦄ :
  Memℒp f p μ → AEStronglyMeasurable' m f μ → P f
MeasureTheory.Memℒp.induction_stronglyMe.comment:
To prove something for an arbitrary `Memℒp` function a.e. strongly measurable with respect
to a sub-σ-algebra `m` in a normed space, it suffices to show that
* the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions which are measurable w.r.t. `m`;
* is closed under addition;
* the set of functions in the `Lᵖ` space strongly measurable w.r.t. `m` for which the property
  holds is closed.
* the property is closed under the almost-everywhere equal relation.

measure_theory.mem_ℒp.induction_strongly.code:
MeasureTheory.Memℒp.induction_stronglyMeasurable.{u_1, u_3} {α : Type u_1} {F : Type u_3} {p : ℝ≥0∞}
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] {m m0 : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} [Fact (1 ≤ p)] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (hm : m ≤ m0)
  (hp_ne_top : p ≠ ⊤) (P : (α → F) → Prop)
  (h_ind : ∀ (c : F) ⦃s : Set α⦄, MeasurableSet s → μ s < ⊤ → P (s.indicator fun x => c))
  (h_add :
    ∀ ⦃f g : α → F⦄,
      Disjoint (Function.support f) (Function.support g) →
        Memℒp f p μ → Memℒp g p μ → StronglyMeasurable f → StronglyMeasurable g → P f → P g → P (f + g))
  (h_closed : IsClosed {f | P ↑↑↑f}) (h_ae : ∀ ⦃f g : α → F⦄, f =ᶠ[ae μ] g → Memℒp f p μ → P f → P g) ⦃f : α → F⦄ :
  Memℒp f p μ → AEStronglyMeasurable' m f μ → P f
measure_theory.mem_ℒp.induction_strongly.comment:
To prove something for an arbitrary `Memℒp` function a.e. strongly measurable with respect
to a sub-σ-algebra `m` in a normed space, it suffices to show that
* the property holds for (multiples of) characteristic functions which are measurable w.r.t. `m`;
* is closed under addition;
* the set of functions in the `Lᵖ` space strongly measurable w.r.t. `m` for which the property
  holds is closed.
* the property is closed under the almost-everywhere equal relation.

Let `m` be a sub-σ-algebra of `m0`, `f` an `m0`-measurable function and `g` an `m`-measurable
function, such that their integrals coincide on `m`-measurable sets with finite measure.
Then `∫ x in s, ‖g x‖ ∂μ ≤ ∫ x in s, ‖f x‖ ∂μ` on all `m`-measurable sets with finite measure.

  (hg : StronglyMeasurable g) (hgi : IntegrableOn g s μ)
  (hgf : ∀ (t : Set α), MeasurableSet t → μ t < ⊤ → ∫ (x : α) in t, g x ∂μ = ∫ (x : α) in t, f x ∂μ)
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hμs : μ s ≠ ⊤) : ∫⁻ (x : α) in s, ↑‖g x‖₊ ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ (x : α) in s, ↑‖f x‖₊ ∂μ
measure_theory.lintegral_nnnorm_le_of_fo.comment:
Let `m` be a sub-σ-algebra of `m0`, `f` an `m0`-measurable function and `g` an `m`-measurable
function, such that their integrals coincide on `m`-measurable sets with finite measure.
Then `∫⁻ x in s, ‖g x‖₊ ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x in s, ‖f x‖₊ ∂μ` on all `m`-measurable sets with finite
measure.

MeasureTheory.condexp.comment:
Conditional expectation of a function. It is defined as 0 if any one of the following conditions
is true:
- `m` is not a sub-σ-algebra of `m0`,
- `μ` is not σ-finite with respect to `m`,
- `f` is not integrable.

MeasureTheory.condexp.fullDefinition: noncomputable irreducible_def condexp (m : MeasurableSpace α) {m0 : MeasurableSpace α}     (μ : Measure α) (f : α → F') : α → F' :=   if hm : m ≤ m0 then     if h : SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm) ∧ Integrable f μ then       if StronglyMeasurable[m] f then f       else (@aestronglyMeasurable'_condexpL1 _ _ _ _ _ m m0 μ hm h.1 _).mk         (@condexpL1 _ _ _ _ _ _ _ hm μ h.1 f)     else 0   else 0

measure_theory.condexp.comment:
Conditional expectation of a function. It is defined as 0 if any one of the following conditions
is true:
- `m` is not a sub-σ-algebra of `m0`,
- `μ` is not σ-finite with respect to `m`,
- `f` is not integrable.

MeasureTheory.condexp_def.{u_5, u_6} {α : Type u_5} {F' : Type u_6} [NormedAddCommGroup F'] [NormedSpace ℝ F']
  [CompleteSpace F'] (m : MeasurableSpace α) {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) (f : α → F') :
  μ[f|m] =
    if hm : m ≤ m0 then
      if h : SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm) ∧ Integrable f μ then
        if StronglyMeasurable f then f else AEStronglyMeasurable'.mk ↑↑(condexpL1 hm μ f) ⋯
      else 0
    else 0

everywhere convergence of a sequence of functions implies the convergence of their image by

explanatories.MeasureTheory.condexpL1: This definition introduces the concept of conditional expectation for a function in L1 space, which yields a value of zero if the function is not integrable, while suggesting that a different function-valued conditional expectation might be preferred in many situations.

MeasureTheory.exists_continuous_snorm_su.code:
MeasureTheory.exists_continuous_snorm_sub_le_of_closed.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]
  [TopologicalSpace α] [T4Space α] [BorelSpace α] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {μ : Measure α} {p : ℝ≥0∞}
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [μ.OuterRegular] (hp : p ≠ ⊤) {s u : Set α} (s_closed : IsClosed s) (u_open : IsOpen u)
  (hsu : s ⊆ u) (hs : μ s ≠ ⊤) (c : E) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≠ 0) :
  ∃ f,
    Continuous f ∧
      snorm (fun x => f x - s.indicator (fun _y => c) x) p μ ≤ ε ∧
        (∀ (x : α), ‖f x‖ ≤ ‖c‖) ∧ Function.support f ⊆ u ∧ Memℒp f p μ
MeasureTheory.exists_continuous_snorm_su.comment:
A variant of Urysohn's lemma, `ℒ^p` version, for an outer regular measure `μ`:
consider two sets `s ⊆ u` which are respectively closed and open with `μ s < ∞`, and a vector `c`.
Then one may find a continuous function `f` equal to `c` on `s` and to `0` outside of `u`,
bounded by `‖c‖` everywhere, and such that the `ℒ^p` norm of `f - s.indicator (fun y ↦ c)` is
arbitrarily small. Additionally, this function `f` belongs to `ℒ^p`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.snorm: This definition describes a seminorm for measurable functions that corresponds to different expressions depending on the value of p, including integrating the p-th power of the norm, taking the essential supremum, and being zero for p equal to zero.
explanatories.Set.indicator: The definition describes a function that outputs a specified value for an element if it is in a given set, and returns zero otherwise.
explanatories.Function.support: This definition introduces the support of a function as the set of inputs for which the function does not map to the additive identity.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.Memℒp: This definition characterizes a property of functions that indicates they are almost everywhere strongly measurable and integrates their norms to a finite value under a measure for finite exponents, or that their essential supremum is finite for the infinite exponent case.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.indic: If a function is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a measure, then the indicator function of a measurable set defined by this function is also almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to the same measure.

MeasureTheory.exists_continuous_snorm_su.description: For given closed and open sets with finite measure, it is possible to find a continuous function that equals a specified constant on the closed set, approaches zero outside the open set, is bounded by the constant, and has a small ℒ^p norm difference from a specific indicator function.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.L2.inner_def: The theorem defines the inner product of two functions in the L2 space as the integral of their inner product evaluated pointwise with respect to the given measure.

explanatories.integral_conj: This theorem states that the integral of a function transformed by a specific endomorphism is equal to the transformation of the integral of that function.
explanatories.inner_conj_symm: This theorem demonstrates that in an inner product space, the inner product is conjugate symmetric, meaning that the inner product of one vector with another is equal to the complex conjugate of the inner product of the latter with the former.
explanatories._private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli: The theorem establishes that the inner product of the sum of two functions in the L2 space with a third function is equal to the sum of their individual inner products with that third function.

MeasureTheory.L2.innerProductSpace.fullDefinition: instance innerProductSpace : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (α →₂[μ] E) where   norm_sq_eq_inner := norm_sq_eq_inner'   conj_symm _ _ := by simp_rw [inner_def, ← integral_conj, inner_conj_symm]   add_left := add_left'   smul_left := smul_left'
MeasureTheory.L2.innerProductSpace.description: This definition establishes a structure where the L2 space of measurable functions with respect to a measure forms an inner product space over a specified field.

MeasureTheory.BoundedContinuousFunction..code:
MeasureTheory.BoundedContinuousFunction.inner_toLp.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [TopologicalSpace α]
  [MeasurableSpace α] [BorelSpace α] [RCLike 𝕜] (μ : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (f g : α →ᵇ 𝕜) :
  ⟪(BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp 2 μ 𝕜) f, (BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp 2 μ 𝕜) g⟫_𝕜 =
    ∫ (x : α), (starRingEnd 𝕜) (f x) * g x ∂μ
MeasureTheory.BoundedContinuousFunction..comment:
For bounded continuous functions `f`, `g` on a finite-measure topological space `α`, the L^2
inner product is the integral of their pointwise inner product.

exists_closed_cover_approximatesLinearOn.code:
exists_closed_cover_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [SecondCountableTopology F] (f : E → F) (s : Set E) (f' : E → E →L[ℝ] F)
  (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x) (r : (E →L[ℝ] F) → ℝ≥0) (rpos : ∀ (A : E →L[ℝ] F), r A ≠ 0) :
  ∃ t A,
    (∀ (n : ℕ), IsClosed (t n)) ∧
      s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ), ApproximatesLinearOn f (A n) (s ∩ t n) (r (A n))) ∧ (s.Nonempty → ∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ y ∈ s, A n = f' y)
exists_closed_cover_approximatesLinearOn.comment:
Assume that a function `f` has a derivative at every point of a set `s`. Then one may cover `s`
with countably many closed sets `t n` on which `f` is well approximated by linear maps `A n`.

explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.HasFDerivWithinAt: A function has a specified continuous linear derivative at a point within a set if its behavior around that point can be approximated by the linear map in the limit as the input approaches the point from within the set.
explanatories.ApproximatesLinearOn: This definition describes a condition under which a function approximates a continuous linear map within a specified set and with a given constant, ensuring the difference between the function's behavior and that of the linear map is proportionally bounded by the distance between points in that set.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.

exists_closed_cover_approximatesLinearOn.description: The theorem asserts that if a function has a derivative at every point of a given set, then it can be approximated by linear maps on a countable collection of closed sets that cover the original set.

MeasureTheory.map_withDensity_abs_det_fd.code:
MeasureTheory.map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {s : Set E} {f : E → E} {f' : E → E →L[ℝ] E} [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  (μ : Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) s x)
  (hf : InjOn f s) (h'f : Measurable f) :
  Measure.map f ((μ.restrict s).withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal |(f' x).det|) = μ.restrict (f '' s)
MeasureTheory.map_withDensity_abs_det_fd.comment:
Change of variable formula for differentiable functions, set version: if a function `f` is
injective and differentiable on a measurable set `s`, then the pushforward of the measure with
density `|(f' x).det|` on `s` is the Lebesgue measure on the image set. This version requires
that `f` is measurable, as otherwise `Measure.map f` is zero per our definitions.
For a version without measurability assumption but dealing with the restricted
function `s.restrict f`, see `restrict_map_withDensity_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar`.

VitaliFamily.covering.code:
VitaliFamily.covering.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α}
  (self : VitaliFamily μ) (s : Set α) (f : α → Set (Set α)) :
  (∀ x ∈ s, f x ⊆ self.setsAt x) →
    (∀ x ∈ s, ∀ ε > 0, ∃ a ∈ f x, a ⊆ closedBall x ε) →
      ∃ t, (∀ p ∈ t, p.1 ∈ s) ∧ (t.PairwiseDisjoint fun p => p.2) ∧ (∀ p ∈ t, p.2 ∈ f p.1) ∧ μ (s \ ⋃ p ∈ t, p.2) = 0
VitaliFamily.covering.comment:
Consider a (possibly non-measurable) set `s`,
and for any `x` in `s` a subfamily `f x` of `setsAt x`
containing sets of arbitrarily small diameter.
Then one can extract a disjoint subfamily covering almost all `s`.

VitaliFamily.FineSubfamilyOn.code:
VitaliFamily.FineSubfamilyOn.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α}
  (v : VitaliFamily μ) (f : α → Set (Set α)) (s : Set α) : Prop
VitaliFamily.FineSubfamilyOn.comment:
Given a Vitali family `v` for a measure `μ`, a family `f` is a fine subfamily on a set `s` if
every point `x` in `s` belongs to arbitrarily small sets in `v.setsAt x ∩ f x`. This is precisely
the subfamilies for which the Vitali family definition ensures that one can extract a disjoint
covering of almost all `s`.

VitaliFamily.FineSubfamilyOn.fullDefinition: def FineSubfamilyOn (v : VitaliFamily μ) (f : α → Set (Set α)) (s : Set α) : Prop :=   ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ ε > 0, ∃ a ∈ v.setsAt x ∩ f x, a ⊆ closedBall x ε
VitaliFamily.FineSubfamilyOn.description: A family of sets is considered a fine subfamily on a given set if every point in that set can be covered by arbitrarily small sets from the intersection of the Vitali family and the family of sets.

VitaliFamily.enlarge.code:
VitaliFamily.enlarge.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} (v : VitaliFamily μ)
  (δ : ℝ) (δpos : 0 < δ) : VitaliFamily μ
VitaliFamily.enlarge.comment:
One can enlarge a Vitali family by adding to the sets `f x` at `x` all sets which are not
contained in a `δ`-neighborhood on `x`. This does not change the local filter at a point, but it
can be convenient to get a nicer global behavior.

explanatories.Metric.closedBall: The closed ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space consists of all points whose distance from that point is less than or equal to a specified radius.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.

explanatories.VitaliFamily.nonempty_interior: Any set in the Vitali family centered at a given point in a metric space has a nonempty interior.

VitaliFamily.enlarge.fullDefinition: def enlarge (v : VitaliFamily μ) (δ : ℝ) (δpos : 0 < δ) : VitaliFamily μ where   setsAt x := v.setsAt x ∪ { a | MeasurableSet a ∧ (interior a).Nonempty ∧ ¬a ⊆ closedBall x δ }   measurableSet x a ha := by     cases' ha with ha ha     exacts [v.measurableSet _ _ ha, ha.1]   nonempty_interior x a ha := by     cases' ha with ha ha     exacts [v.nonempty_interior _ _ ha, ha.2.1]   nontrivial := by     intro x ε εpos     rcases v.nontrivial x ε εpos with ⟨a, ha, h'a⟩     exact ⟨a, mem_union_left _ ha, h'a⟩   covering := by     intro s f fset ffine     let g : α → Set (Set α) := fun x => f x ∩ v.setsAt x     have : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ ε : ℝ, ε > 0 → ∃ (a : Set α), a ∈ g x ∧ a ⊆ closedBall x ε := by       intro x hx ε εpos       obtain ⟨a, af, ha⟩ : ∃ a ∈ f x, a ⊆ closedBall x (min ε δ) :=         ffine x hx (min ε δ) (lt_min εpos δpos)       rcases fset x hx af with (h'a | h'a)       · exact ⟨a, ⟨af, h'a⟩, ha.trans (closedBall_subset_closedBall (min_le_left _ _))⟩       · refine False.elim (h'a.2.2 ?_)         exact ha.trans (closedBall_subset_closedBall (min_le_right _ _))     rcases v.covering s g (fun x _ => inter_subset_right) this with ⟨t, ts, tdisj, tg, μt⟩     exact ⟨t, ts, tdisj, fun p hp => (tg p hp).1, μt⟩
VitaliFamily.enlarge.description: This definition allows for the enlargement of a Vitali family by including additional sets outside a specified neighborhood around each point, enhancing the family's global properties while maintaining its local structure.

VitaliFamily.filterAt.code:
VitaliFamily.filterAt.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} (v : VitaliFamily μ)
  (x : α) : Filter (Set α)
VitaliFamily.filterAt.comment:
Given a vitali family `v`, then `v.filterAt x` is the filter on `Set α` made of those families
that contain all sets of `v.setsAt x` of a sufficiently small diameter. This filter makes it
possible to express limiting behavior when sets in `v.setsAt x` shrink to `x`.

explanatories.VitaliFamily.setsAt: This definition describes a function that assigns to each point in a metric space the sets from a Vitali family that are centered at that point.
explanatories.Filter.smallSets: The largest filter consisting of all the powersets of the elements in a given filter is defined as the small sets filter of that original filter.
explanatories.Filter.HasBasis.smallSets: The small sets filter of a given filter that has a basis is also shown to have a basis formed by the powersets of the sets corresponding to that basis.

VitaliFamily.filterAt.fullDefinition: def filterAt (x : α) : Filter (Set α) := (𝓝 x).smallSets ⊓ 𝓟 (v.setsAt x)
VitaliFamily.filterAt.description: This definition describes a filter on sets that includes all sufficiently small sets from a Vitali family centered at a specific point, enabling the analysis of limiting behavior as these sets shrink towards that point.

Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_coverin.code:
Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargment.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} (B : ι → Set α)
  (t : Set ι) (δ : ι → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (hτ : 1 < τ) (δnonneg : ∀ a ∈ t, 0 ≤ δ a) (R : ℝ) (δle : ∀ a ∈ t, δ a ≤ R)
  (hne : ∀ a ∈ t, (B a).Nonempty) :
  ∃ u ⊆ t, u.PairwiseDisjoint B ∧ ∀ a ∈ t, ∃ b ∈ u, (B a ∩ B b).Nonempty ∧ δ a ≤ τ * δ b
Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_coverin.comment:
**Vitali covering theorem**: given a set `t` of subsets of a type, one may extract a disjoint
subfamily `u` such that the `τ`-enlargment of this family covers all elements of `t`, where `τ > 1`
is any fixed number.

When `t` is a family of balls, the `τ`-enlargment of `ball x r` is `ball x ((1+2τ) r)`. In general,
it is expressed in terms of a function `δ` (think "radius" or "diameter"), positive and bounded on
all elements of `t`. The condition is that every element `a` of `t` should intersect an
element `b` of `u` of size larger than that of `a` up to `τ`, i.e., `δ b ≥ δ a / τ`.

We state the lemma slightly more generally, with an indexed family of sets `B a` for `a ∈ t`, for
wider applicability.

  (t : Set ι) (x : ι → α) (r : ι → ℝ) (R : ℝ) (hr : ∀ a ∈ t, r a ≤ R) :

Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae.code:
Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [MetricSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace α] [SecondCountableTopology α] (μ : Measure α) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (s : Set α)
  (t : Set ι) (C : ℝ≥0) (r : ι → ℝ) (c : ι → α) (B : ι → Set α) (hB : ∀ a ∈ t, B a ⊆ closedBall (c a) (r a))
  (μB : ∀ a ∈ t, μ (closedBall (c a) (3 * r a)) ≤ ↑C * μ (B a)) (ht : ∀ a ∈ t, (interior (B a)).Nonempty)
  (h't : ∀ a ∈ t, IsClosed (B a)) (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ ε > 0, ∃ a ∈ t, r a ≤ ε ∧ c a = x) :
  ∃ u ⊆ t, u.Countable ∧ u.PairwiseDisjoint B ∧ μ (s \ ⋃ a ∈ u, B a) = 0
Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae.comment:
The measurable Vitali covering theorem. Assume one is given a family `t` of closed sets with
nonempty interior, such that each `a ∈ t` is included in a ball `B (x, r)` and covers a definite
proportion of the ball `B (x, 3 r)` for a given measure `μ` (think of the situation where `μ` is
a doubling measure and `t` is a family of balls). Consider a (possibly non-measurable) set `s`
at which the family is fine, i.e., every point of `s` belongs to arbitrarily small elements of `t`.
Then one can extract from `t` a disjoint subfamily that covers almost all `s`.

For more flexibility, we give a statement with a parameterized family of sets.

Vitali.vitaliFamily.code:
Vitali.vitaliFamily.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α]
  [SecondCountableTopology α] (μ : Measure α) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (C : ℝ≥0)
  (h : ∀ (x : α), ∃ᶠ (r : ℝ) in 𝓝[>] 0, μ (closedBall x (3 * r)) ≤ ↑C * μ (closedBall x r)) : VitaliFamily μ
Vitali.vitaliFamily.comment:
Assume that around every point there are arbitrarily small scales at which the measure is
doubling. Then the set of closed sets `a` with nonempty interior contained in `closedBall x r` and
covering a fixed proportion `1/C` of the ball `closedBall x (3 * r)` forms a Vitali family.
This is essentially a restatement of the measurable Vitali theorem.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Metric.closedBall: The closed ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space consists of all points whose distance from that point is less than or equal to a specified radius.
explanatories.Set.Subset.rfl: Every set is a subset of itself.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty.mono: If a non-empty set is a subset of another set, then the larger set is also non-empty.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Set.Countable.mono: If one set is a subset of another countable set, then the first set is also countable.
explanatories.IsClosed.measurableSet: A closed set in a topological space that has an opens measurable space structure is also a measurable set.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.exists: A theorem stating that if a property holds for almost all elements in a non-empty filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property holds.
explanatories.SetCoe.exists: The existence of an element satisfying a property in a set is equivalent to the existence of an element in that set whose image under a coercion also satisfies the property.
explanatories.Metric.closedBall_subset_closedBall: The closed ball around a point with a smaller radius is contained within the closed ball around the same point with a larger radius.
explanatories.min_le_left: This theorem establishes that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the first element.
explanatories.min_le_right: This theorem demonstrates that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the second element.
explanatories.Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae: From a given family of closed sets with specific properties, one can extract a countable, pairwise disjoint subfamily that covers almost all points in a specified set while reflecting a controlled measure.
explanatories.Set.Ioc: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-open and right-closed interval.
explanatories.Filter.Frequently.and_eventually: A theorem asserting that if a property holds frequently for a filter and another property holds eventually for the same filter, then there exists a set of elements for which both properties hold frequently.
explanatories.Ioc_mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi: This theorem states that if a point is within a closed interval, then the open interval around two endpoints contains the neighborhood of that point when considering neighborhoods to the right.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.Filter.Frequently.exists: A theorem stating that if a property holds frequently in a filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property is true.
explanatories.Metric.isClosed_ball: The closed ball around a point in a pseudometric space is a closed set.
explanatories.Metric.nonempty_ball: The non-empty nature of the set of points within a specified distance from a point in a pseudo-metric space depends on that distance being positive.
explanatories.Metric.ball_subset_interior_closedBall: The open ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space is contained within the interior of the closed ball around the same point with the same radius.

⟨q, hq, rfl⟩       exact (t't hq).2.2.2.2.2     · rintro p ⟨q, hq, rfl⟩ p' ⟨q', hq', rfl⟩ hqq'       exact t'_disj hq hq' (ne_of_apply_ne _ hqq')     · rintro - ⟨q, hq, rfl⟩       exact (t't hq).2.2.2.2.1     · convert μt' using 3       rw [biUnion_image]
Vitali.vitaliFamily.description: The collection of closed sets with nonempty interior that are contained within a ball and cover a specified proportion of a surrounding ball forms a Vitali family assuming the measure around each point demonstrates a doubling property at arbitrarily small scales.

vitali.vitali_family.code:
Vitali.vitaliFamily.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] [MeasurableSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α]
  [SecondCountableTopology α] (μ : Measure α) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (C : ℝ≥0)
  (h : ∀ (x : α), ∃ᶠ (r : ℝ) in 𝓝[>] 0, μ (closedBall x (3 * r)) ≤ ↑C * μ (closedBall x r)) : VitaliFamily μ
vitali.vitali_family.comment:
Assume that around every point there are arbitrarily small scales at which the measure is
doubling. Then the set of closed sets `a` with nonempty interior contained in `closedBall x r` and
covering a fixed proportion `1/C` of the ball `closedBall x (3 * r)` forms a Vitali family.
This is essentially a restatement of the measurable Vitali theorem.

explanatories.Filter.Frequently.exists: A theorem stating that if a property holds frequently in a filter, then there exists at least one element for which the property is true.

VitaliFamily.limRatio.code:
VitaliFamily.limRatio.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} (v : VitaliFamily μ)
  (ρ : Measure α) (x : α) : ℝ≥0∞
VitaliFamily.limRatio.comment:
The limit along a Vitali family of `ρ a / μ a` where it makes sense, and garbage otherwise.
Do *not* use this definition: it is only a temporary device to show that this ratio tends almost
everywhere to the Radon-Nikodym derivative.

explanatories.limUnder: The limit of a function at a given filter is defined as the point in the topological space that the function approaches under the conditions specified by that filter, provided such a limit exists.
explanatories.VitaliFamily.filterAt: This definition describes a filter on sets that includes all sufficiently small sets from a Vitali family centered at a specific point, enabling the analysis of limiting behavior as these sets shrink towards that point.

VitaliFamily.limRatio.fullDefinition: noncomputable def limRatio (ρ : Measure α) (x : α) : ℝ≥0∞ :=   limUnder (v.filterAt x) fun a => ρ a / μ a
VitaliFamily.limRatio.description: The limit of the ratio between two measures along a Vitali family is defined for almost every point and acts as a temporary construct, suggesting convergence to the Radon-Nikodym derivative.

VitaliFamily.ae_eventually_measure_pos.comment:
For almost every point `x`, sufficiently small sets in a Vitali family around `x` have positive
measure. (This is a nontrivial result, following from the covering property of Vitali families).

  [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ν] (hρ : ρ ≪ μ) (s : Set α) (hs : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ᶠ (a : Set α) in v.filterAt x, ρ a ≤ ν a) :

VitaliFamily.measure_le_of_frequently_le.comment:
If two measures `ρ` and `ν` have, at every point of a set `s`, arbitrarily small sets in a
Vitali family satisfying `ρ a ≤ ν a`, then `ρ s ≤ ν s` if `ρ ≪ μ`.

VitaliFamily.ae_eventually_measure_zero_.code:
VitaliFamily.ae_eventually_measure_zero_of_singular.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α}
  {μ : Measure α} (v : VitaliFamily μ) [SecondCountableTopology α] [BorelSpace α] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
  {ρ : Measure α} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ρ] (hρ : ρ ⟂ₘ μ) :
  ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, Tendsto (fun a => ρ a / μ a) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 0)
VitaliFamily.ae_eventually_measure_zero_.comment:
If a measure `ρ` is singular with respect to `μ`, then for `μ` almost every `x`, the ratio
`ρ a / μ a` tends to zero when `a` shrinks to `x` along the Vitali family. This makes sense
as `μ a` is eventually positive by `ae_eventually_measure_pos`.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.

VitaliFamily.ae_eventually_measure_zero_.description: If one measure is singular with respect to another, then almost every point results in the ratio of the two measures tending to zero as the sets shrink towards that point within a Vitali family.

VitaliFamily.null_of_frequently_le_of_fr.code:
VitaliFamily.null_of_frequently_le_of_frequently_ge.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α}
  {μ : Measure α} (v : VitaliFamily μ) [SecondCountableTopology α] [BorelSpace α] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
  {ρ : Measure α} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ρ] (hρ : ρ ≪ μ) {c d : ℝ≥0} (hcd : c < d) (s : Set α)
  (hc : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ᶠ (a : Set α) in v.filterAt x, ρ a ≤ ↑c * μ a)
  (hd : ∀ x ∈ s, ∃ᶠ (a : Set α) in v.filterAt x, ↑d * μ a ≤ ρ a) : μ s = 0
VitaliFamily.null_of_frequently_le_of_fr.comment:
A set of points `s` satisfying both `ρ a ≤ c * μ a` and `ρ a ≥ d * μ a` at arbitrarily small
sets in a Vitali family has measure `0` if `c < d`. Indeed, the first inequality should imply
that `ρ s ≤ c * μ s`, and the second one that `ρ s ≥ d * μ s`, a contradiction if `0 < μ s`.

VitaliFamily.null_of_frequently_le_of_fr.description: If a set of points meets the criteria of having both the measures being bounded above and below by different positive constants in small sets from a Vitali family, then the measure of that set must be zero.

A set of points `s` satisfying both `ρ a ≤ c * μ a` and `ρ a ≥ d * μ a` at arbitrarily small
sets in a Vitali family has measure `0` if `c < d`. Indeed, the first inequality should imply
that `ρ s ≤ c * μ s`, and the second one that `ρ s ≥ d * μ s`, a contradiction if `0 < μ s`.

VitaliFamily.exists_measurable_supersets_limRatio.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α}
  {μ : Measure α} (v : VitaliFamily μ) [SecondCountableTopology α] [BorelSpace α] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
  {ρ : Measure α} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ρ] (hρ : ρ ≪ μ) {p q : ℝ≥0} (hpq : p < q) :
  ∃ a b,
    MeasurableSet a ∧ MeasurableSet b ∧ {x | v.limRatio ρ x < ↑p} ⊆ a ∧ {x | ↑q < v.limRatio ρ x} ⊆ b ∧ μ (a ∩ b) = 0
VitaliFamily.exists_measurable_supersets.comment:
Given two thresholds `p < q`, the sets `{x | v.limRatio ρ x < p}`
and `{x | q < v.limRatio ρ x}` are obviously disjoint. The key to proving that `v.limRatio ρ` is
almost everywhere measurable is to show that these sets have measurable supersets which are also
disjoint, up to zero measure. This is the content of this lemma.

VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv_of_absolutelyContinuous.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MetricSpace α] {m0 : MeasurableSpace α}
  {μ : Measure α} (v : VitaliFamily μ) [SecondCountableTopology α] [BorelSpace α] [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
  {ρ : Measure α} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ρ] (hρ : ρ ≪ μ) :
  ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, Tendsto (fun a => ρ a / μ a) (v.filterAt x) (𝓝 (ρ.rnDeriv μ x))
VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv_of_absol.comment:
Weak version of the main theorem on differentiation of measures: given a Vitali family `v`
for a locally finite measure `μ`, and another locally finite measure `ρ`, then for `μ`-almost
every `x` the ratio `ρ a / μ a` converges, when `a` shrinks to `x` along the Vitali family,
towards the Radon-Nikodym derivative of `ρ` with respect to `μ`.

This version assumes that `ρ` is absolutely continuous with respect to `μ`. The general version
without this superfluous assumption is `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv`.

explanatories.MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv: This definition describes a measurable function that represents the Radon-Nikodym derivative of one measure with respect to another, returning this derivative function or the zero function if no decomposition exists.

VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_di.comment:
Given a measurable set `s`, then `μ (s ∩ a) / μ a` converges when `a` shrinks to a typical
point `x` along a Vitali family. The limit is `1` for `x ∈ s` and `0` for `x ∉ s`. This shows that
almost every point of `s` is a Lebesgue density point for `s`. A version for non-measurable sets

  VitaliFamily μ
IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.vitaliFamily.comment:
A Vitali family in a space with a uniformly locally doubling measure, designed so that the sets
at `x` contain all `closedBall y r` when `dist x y ≤ K * r`.

explanatories.IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.scalingScaleOf: This definition introduces a scale that determines the range within which a doubling measure maintains favorable rescaling properties when the radii of balls are multiplied by a specified factor.
explanatories.IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.scalingScaleOf_: This theorem asserts that for a uniformly locally doubling measure, the scaling scale associated with a given constant is positive.
explanatories.IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.scalingConstant: This defines a non-negative scaling constant that applies to a uniformly locally doubling measure, accommodating scaling of the radius by values other than two.
explanatories.Filter.frequently_iff: A theorem stating that the existence of frequently occurring elements in a filter corresponds to the condition that for any set in the filter, there is at least one element from that set that satisfies a given property.
explanatories.mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset: A set is a neighborhood of a point within an open interval if and only if it includes another interval that starts at that point and extends to a point that is greater than or equal to it.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.lt_min: This theorem asserts that if an element is less than two other elements in a linear order, then it is also less than the minimum of those two elements.
explanatories.min_le_left: This theorem establishes that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the first element.
explanatories.IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.measure_mul_le_: This theorem establishes that for a uniformly locally doubling measure, the measure of a closed ball with a scaled radius is bounded above by a product of a scaling constant and the measure of a closed ball with the original radius, provided the scaling factor is within specific limits.
explanatories.zero_lt_three: This theorem asserts that in any partially ordered set that is also an additive monoid with one, zero is less than three.
explanatories.le_max_right: This theorem asserts that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.min_le_right: This theorem demonstrates that the minimum of two elements in a linear order is less than or equal to the second element.
explanatories.Vitali.vitaliFamily: The collection of closed sets with nonempty interior that are contained within a ball and cover a specified proportion of a surrounding ball forms a Vitali family assuming the measure around each point demonstrates a doubling property at arbitrarily small scales.
explanatories.VitaliFamily.enlarge: This definition allows for the enlargement of a Vitali family by including additional sets outside a specified neighborhood around each point, enhancing the family's global properties while maintaining its local structure.
explanatories.Subtype.property: This theorem states that for any element of a subtype defined by a property, that element satisfies the property itself.
explanatories.Filter.Eventually.and: A theorem stating that if two properties hold eventually with respect to a filter, then their conjunction also holds eventually with respect to that filter.

IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.vitaliFamily.fullDefinition: irreducible_def vitaliFamily (K : ℝ) : VitaliFamily μ := by   /- the Vitali covering theorem gives a family that works well at small scales, thanks to the     doubling property. We enlarge this family to add large sets, to make sure that all balls and not     only small ones belong to the family, for convenience. -/   let R := scalingScaleOf μ (max (4 * K + 3) 3)   have Rpos : 0 < R := scalingScaleOf_pos _ _   have A : ∀ x : α, ∃ᶠ r in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),       μ (closedBall x (3 * r)) ≤ scalingConstantOf μ (max (4 * K + 3) 3) * μ (closedBall x r) := by     intro x     apply frequently_iff.2 fun {U} hU => ?_     obtain ⟨ε, εpos, hε⟩ := mem_nhdsWithin_Ioi_iff_exists_Ioc_subset.1 hU     refine ⟨min ε R, hε ⟨lt_min εpos Rpos, min_le_left _ _⟩, ?_⟩     exact measure_mul_le_scalingConstantOf_mul μ       ⟨zero_lt_three, le_max_right _ _⟩ (min_le_right _ _)   exact (Vitali.vitaliFamily μ (scalingConstantOf μ (max (4 * K + 3) 3)) A).enlarge (R / 4)     (by linarith)
IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.vitaliFamily.description: A Vitali family is established in a space with a uniformly locally doubling measure, ensuring that sets around each point include all closed balls when the distance to another point is proportional to the radius of the ball.
